title: Pre-green stop budget sweep — measure Steve's actual stop doctrine, which nothing has tested
description:
## Why this exists

Steve withdrew 'zero-tolerance stop' as overstated on 2026-08-09. His actual doctrine: **until P/L is green, avoid drawdown beyond ~3 points; after green, tolerance widens but bounded, traded off against probability of profit.**

Nothing has tested that. What st-gzwb refuted was zero-tolerance and near-noise-floor cuts — FD0's ~1.1-pt budget-derived stop measured roughly 3x INSIDE the noise floor. Separately measured: at 2-pt backtests the move resumes 96-98%. A 3-pt pre-green stop sits just OUTSIDE that common backtest band. Different animal, never measured, and it is now the main line of the program (charter: knowledge/counter-dictum-program.md sections 4a and 6).

## What to measure

On the 22-day morning-flush corpus and the 63-day 1s archive, both already on disk:

1. **Pre-green budget sweep**: 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 SPX points, hard stop while position is red.
2. **Post-green rule sweep**, crossed with the above: (a) stop to breakeven at green, (b) trail by N points, (c) widen to a fixed larger budget, (d) no change (control).
3. **Both entry geometries**: breakout (st-gzwb baseline) and join-the-turn on bar closes (st-chat), so entry and stop are graded as the pair section 4.0 of the charter requires.
4. **Friction is decisive at this scale — model it explicitly.** The st-gzwb study used 0.6 SPX pts/attempt. Against a 3-pt pre-green budget that is ~20% of the budget consumed per attempt. Report results both raw and friction-adjusted; if liberal re-entry dies on friction alone, that is the finding.
5. **Express the stop in the traded instrument, not just SPX points.** 3 SPX points through a 0.30-delta single is ~$0.90 of option price against a typical 0DTE bid/ask. State the spread assumption; test an ITM variant, since knowledge/singles-as-futures-proxy already prescribes leaning ITM for tighter delta and spread.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Results table: median and mean net points/day, attempts/day, days positive, per (pre-green budget x post-green rule x entry geometry), raw and friction-adjusted
- Channel-family verdicts written BEFORE measuring, per knowledge/channel-family-taxonomy — including a clock verdict, since hour-of-day baselines differ 77% vs 25% (st-1bv1) and must be the comparator
- Explicit verdict on whether any cell beats the oracle-direction endure baseline (+18.5 pts/day median, st-gzwb)
- Artifact guard: assert attempts/day < 50 in every config, else report as churn artifact not as a number
- Dated section in docs/measurement/ + desk render; raw output in data/derived/
- States plainly whether Steve's 3-pt doctrine survives, and if not, at what budget it starts to

title: Counter-dictum program charter — one canonical statement of what we are trying to do and why, reachable from every session
description:
## The problem

Steve, 2026-08-09: 'we need to arrange/configure memories of our current focus so that everyone has a common understanding of what we are trying to do and why.'

Verified this session: **every memory store in this enterprise is per-repo.** Beads issues (st-ygy1 is invisible from COO), `bd remember` (COO holds 8 keys, Strader 4, no overlap), Claude auto-memory (`~/.claude/projects/-root-projects-<repo>/memory/`), CLAUDE.md, and the OKF bundles are all repo-scoped. Cross-repo READS are permitted and free; nothing is shared by default.

Consequence, measured not assumed: the counter-dictum program's *purpose* lives only in COO's private auto-memory (project_orderflow-mastery-directive, project_singleton-scalp-proxy-target, project_execution-harness-exploration). Strader's auto-memory index carries neither the directive nor the singleton redirect. The domain that executes the work cannot see why it is being done.

Two failures already trace to this:
1. COO drifted toward fly-lane assistance, requiring Steve's 2026-08-08 singleton-scalp-proxy correction.
2. The bundle concept 'Channel Family Taxonomy' (st-a3yh) named CLOCK the strongest predictor found (day-median AUC .875) AND marked it NEVER-TRAVERSED, with a binding traverse-before-measuring procedure. Four orderflow edge-test rounds ignored it. Hour-of-day then beat every signal those rounds produced (st-1bv1).

## Design

**One canonical charter, pointers on every always-loaded surface.** No content copies — copies drift, proven twice in this bundle's own log (tradingview concept named a deleted tool for six weeks; directional-gex-butterflies re-corrected four times because CLAUDE.md outranked it).

- Charter: `Strader/knowledge/counter-dictum-program.md`, type `decision`. Lives here because the work executes here and it must bind to the taxonomy concept already in this bundle.
- Pointer, Strader `bd remember` (injected at every `bd prime`)
- Pointer, COO `bd remember`
- Pointer line, Strader auto-memory MEMORY.md
- COO auto-memory: the three fragment files point at the charter instead of restating it

Charter contents: the goal and Steve's rationale; the target application (singletons as futures-scalp proxy, 5-15 min holds, NOT fly assistance); the scoring rule (directional tail shift against the hour's own baseline, never the pooled 40%); the settled ledger of live-vs-killed; the open disputes; the hard boundaries (human-triggered not automated, SPX only full size, Steve sole risk authority).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Charter exists, typed `decision`, frontmatter complete, listed in knowledge/index.md, bundle log appended citing this bead
- A cold-start session in EITHER repo reaches the charter from an always-loaded surface without Steve saying anything
- Charter carries the binding study-design rule (traverse channel families before measuring; score against the hour's own baseline) — the enforcement layer that was missing
- No content duplicated between repos; pointers only
- COO's three fragment memories reconciled to the charter, not left as rival statements

title: Clock family traversal — hour-of-day baseline, and the four orderflow rounds that skipped it
description:
## What happened

On 2026-08-09 Steve challenged a sentence in COO's orderflow state-of-play report claiming the data 'kept pointing at the late-day window' because 83% of giant flow prints land within 30 min of the close. The challenge was correct: that conflated options-flow notional with tradeable price displacement. Measuring both by clock hour over the same 63-day 1s archive (2026-05-07..2026-08-06) settled it.

| CT hour | P(>=10pt move in 15 min) | median 15-min excursion | n windows | fix2000 flow prints |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 08 (from 08:30) | 77% | 14.80 | 1684 | 2 |
| 09 | 62% | 11.67 | 3505 | 4 |
| 10 | 42% | 8.88 | 3537 | 6 |
| 11 | 32% | 7.33 | 3545 | 7 |
| 12 | 26% | 6.67 | 3551 | 11 |
| 13 | 25% | 6.09 | 3548 | 35 |
| 14 | 27% | 6.66 | 2655 | 4743 |

97% of giant flow prints (4679/4808) fall in the final 30 minutes, where displacement is at its daily floor — expiry mechanics (0DTE settlement, closing-auction hedging, vanna/charm unwind) moving notional without moving price. Absolute excursion either direction: opportunity, not directional edge.

## Why this is P1

The Strader bundle concept 'Channel Family Taxonomy' (st-a3yh) already records CLOCK as the strongest single predictor the continuation audit found (day-median AUC .875 vs the deliverable's .607) AND as a NEVER-TRAVERSED family. Its procedure is binding: a study design opens by traversing the family list and writing a verdict per family BEFORE measuring. Orderflow edge-test rounds 1-4 (st-yirc, st-mvvf, st-gkbo, st-a2cj) did not do that. The bundle named the answer; nobody read it. This bead exists so the traversal is recorded rather than rediscovered a third time.

Consequence for the program: round 4's pooled baseline (>=10pt move in ~40% of 15-min windows) averages across a 77%-to-25% gradient. Every orderflow candidate scored against that flat number was scored against the wrong comparator, and hour-of-day outperforms every signal four rounds produced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Hour-of-day table written into docs/measurement/ as a dated finding, raw output alongside it, reproduction script committed
- 'Channel Family Taxonomy' concept updated: clock family verdict moves from NEVER-TRAVERSED to measured, citing this result
- Bundle log entry appended citing this bead
- Round 4's pooled ~40% baseline explicitly retired as a comparator in the measurement record; future candidates score against their own hour
- Read-through to st-v5a8 (10:00-13:00 no-trade window) noted: >=10pt probability falls 42/32/26 across that span — evidence for the window, but excursion is not tradeability and the directional/cost sides are still owed

title: Strader: gexbot-hist files are named .json.gz but are plain JSON — 56G uncompressed, landmine for the retro cut
description:
scripts/gexbot_hist_backfill.py writes `blob.content` straight to
data/corpus/gexbot-hist/<date>/<package>_<category>.json.gz. requests already
transparently decodes Content-Encoding: gzip, so `.content` is DECOMPRESSED
bytes. Every file on disk is plain ASCII JSON wearing a .gz extension.

Verified 2026-08-05 at tap-in: `file` reports "ASCII text, with very long
lines" on both a completed day (2026-06-24) and the interrupted day
(2026-06-25); `gzip -t` reports "not in gzip format".

Two consequences:

1. LANDMINE. Nothing reads these yet — the retro gamma cut (st-trbn) is the
   first consumer. Five existing modules in this repo use gzip.open() on
   corpus files (live_footprint_feed, corpus_compact_databento,
   orderflow/quotes, measurement/fly, corpus/paths), so the house pattern is
   gzip.open. The first author to follow that pattern gets an unreadable
   file and a confusing traceback, not a clear error.

2. SIZE. 56G for 37 of 90 days uncompressed. Full window lands ~135G on top
   of a corpus already at 148G. Disk is fine (768G free), so this is not
   urgent capacity pressure — it is waste and a mislabel.

## Decide between

- Compress on write (gzip.compress before write_bytes) and keep the name.
  Correct long-term; requires a one-time recompression pass over the 37 days
  already fetched, and the resume run must not re-download them.
- Rename to .json and leave uncompressed. Cheapest, honest, costs the disk.

Prefer the first, but the backfill must be RESUMED before this is touched —
the run is stopped 2/3 through a paid one-month window and finishing it is
worth more than the storage.

## Do not

Re-fetch anything already on disk to fix this. The data is good; only the
container is wrong.

title: GexBot reactivation: key-live probe + 90-day historical backfill
description:

The API spec (docs/gexbot/gexbot.spec3.yaml:249) defines /hist/{ticker}/{package}/{category}/{date} — pre-signed URL download of a day's data (JSON, gzip), 90-day rolling look-back, tagged 'Quant'. Whether State tier includes it is UNVERIFIED — no tier-gating info in the May docs extraction. Steve will report what the subscribe page says; first probe confirms.

## Steps
1. python3 scripts/gexbot_probe.py — keyed endpoints must return 200 (401 = still paused, stop)
2. Probe /hist/SPX/state/gamma_zero/<yesterday> with noredirect — confirm access + inspect payload granularity
3. Backfill loop: all available dates (~90 back) for SPX: state/gamma_zero, classic/gex_zero + majors. Store data/corpus/gexbot-hist/<date>/*.json.gz. Rate-limit ≥1.1s between calls (matches gexbot_stream.py spacing).

5. Delete the stale pause memory /root/.claude/projects/-root-projects-Strader/memory/project_gexbot_paused.md (its own instruction: delete when reactivated)

The look-back window rolls daily: each day of delay permanently loses the oldest day of joinable GEX history. The retro gamma-cut of the acuity corpus (follow-on bead) depends on maximum overlap.

title: Watcher validation gap — no meter journal exists for a real flush day

title: Flush watcher — meter journal to phone alert, shadow-mode first
description:
Steve 2026-08-05: 'proceed as if it worked and wire into the watcher (or whatever component is responsible)'. FINDING: the FD0 watcher does not exist — st-apzt is design-only, no watcher module in the tree. The component that actually runs live and observes the market is scripts/desk/continuation_meter.py (30s poll, primary-move detection, journals every frame). So the watcher consumes the meter's journal: meter observes, watcher decides, strader.alerts fires. Loose coupling, no second Schwab data path, reuses a proven live leg.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT (audit discipline, 2026-08-04 report): the trigger threshold has NOT been measured. R4 (st-rtuu, Obvious Line Formalization) is the lane that measures it. Therefore this ships in SHADOW MODE by default — it evaluates live, journals every would-fire, and sends NOTHING until --live is passed. An alerting detector on unmeasured thresholds is the cry-wolf failure that gets notifications turned off, which destroys the whole arm.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Consumes the meter journal; no new market-data coupling
- Shadow by default; --live required to actually send; both journal identically
- Rate limits: at most one alert per distinct move, and a hard daily cap
- Alert message carries the fire-server URL so the tap goes straight to the form
- Provisional threshold clearly marked as unmeasured, with the bead that will replace it named in the code
- Tests cover: shadow sends nothing, dedupe per move, daily cap, message content
close_reason:
Delivered scripts/flush_watcher.py + 15 tests (full suite 730 green), commit pushed. Chain: continuation meter observes -> journal -> watcher decides -> strader.alerts fires. No FD0 watcher existed to wire into (st-apzt design-only) and no second market-data path was created — the watcher only reads the meter's journal, so it cannot break the meter.

SHADOW BY DEFAULT; --live required to send. Trigger constants (25 pts, down-only, 08:30-11:00 CT window) are explicitly marked provisional in the code with st-rtuu named as the lane that replaces them. Structural rate limits: one alert per distinct move (keyed on move start), hard daily cap of 3, stale meter frames (>5 min) refused as evidence. Quiet frames journal their reason so a shadow run produces evidence rather than silence.

Replay: 08-04 (1,665 frames) and 08-05 (178) -> 0 would-alerts. Both up days, trigger is down-only, so this proves no-false-positives-on-up-days and nothing more. Validation gap filed as Watcher Validation Gap (st-88ei): the real flush tapes are 07-22/07-31 and the meter journal only starts 08-03, so a synthetic meter-frame generator from corpus tape is needed before any --live run.

title: Exit-all panic button — flatten every position from the phone
description:

- The KILL SWITCH MUST NOT BLOCK EXIT. FIRE_DISABLED stops the machine ENTERING trades; if it also blocked exits it would trap Steve in positions at the worst moment — exactly backwards. Kill switch blocks entries only; exit-all always available.
- Qty cap and ticket-staleness rails do not apply — exit acts on live account state, not a staged ticket.
- Two-step (EXIT ALL -> confirm w/ nonce) kept: one extra tap beats a pocket-tap flattening the book. Exit is lower-risk than entry (worst case: flat when you did not want to be), so no further ceremony.
- Phase 2 order type: MARKET to close. Certainty of exit beats price improvement in a panic; noted as the wide-spread tradeoff for Steve's ruling.

Phase 1 (this bead): button + confirm + rails + journal, DRY-RUN. Cannot enumerate positions (fork hobbled: no account access) and cannot transmit (no order client) — both stated on-screen rather than faked.

description:

title: Live continuation meter — desk pane grading flush continuation in real time
description:
Steve's direction 2026-08-03: build the live continuation meter pane (the follow-on lane named in docs/measurement/morning-flush-continuation.md).

## What it is
A display-only tmux pane on steves-desk (socket moocity) refreshing every ~30s during RTH:
- Today's primary move so far ($SPX minute closes from 08:30 CT, same max-excursion definition as the study; floor 10 pts before grading)
- The three convergence traces with confirm/deny marks: $TICK on move's side, $ADD 10-min slope, $VIX 5-min slope — score 0-3 mapped to measured P(extend >=2pts, 15min): 25/49/65/73% (July, n=22, morning-window calibration — caveat shown after 10:30)
- Vol-complex quadrant (VIX x VVIX 5-min signs) with named states: complex-bid 74%, death rattle 31% (up move, complex bid against it), fuel gone 47% (down move, complex releasing)
- ES x VIX bounce-not-believed state when applicable (66%)
- Context line: VIX / VVIX / 9D-30D spread levels
- Freshness guard: newest internals candle older than 3 min => loud STALE line, never silently wrong numbers
- Journal every refresh to data/exec/continuation-meter-<day>.jsonl

## Not in scope
No orders, no order strings, no coupling to FD0 state; display only. Not automated re-entry (st-ug5 boundary: human trigger).

## Mechanics
Data via broker_schwab get_price_history_every_minute for $SPX + 5 internals (~12 req/min at 30s cadence, well under limits) + existing token check at startup. Plain-words output (Steve reads the pane; no jargon, no curses UI). Tested with --once live, then launched in the pane via two send-keys calls per convention.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: VIX depth pass — de-seasoned slope, beta residual, quadrant flags, term structure
description:
Steve's direction 2026-08-03 after the continuation-trace review: VIX has no tape (index over SPX option quotes), but structure beyond rising/falling exists. Measure four refinements against the 22 July morning-move days using the st-cdwe labeling (CONT = extends >=2 pts within 15 min; 1,882 minutes):

1. De-seasoned VIX slope — VIX carries mechanical intraday decay (opens rich, drifts down), so raw slope conflates clock with information. Compute per-minute-of-day median 5-min slope across VIX corpus days leave-one-day-out; trace = (raw - seasonal median) x (-dir). Compare AUC vs the raw vix_slope5 (.660) it replaces.
2. Beta residual — fit dVIX_5m = a + b*dES%_5m leave-one-day-out; trace = residual x (-dir): VIX moving MORE than the ES move justifies = protection demand (dn) / vol crush (up). Report fit b and R^2 so the expected-response claim is cited, not asserted.
3. Quadrant flags — sign(dES_5m) x sign(dVIX_5m) quadrant occupancy and P(CONT) per quadrant conditioned on move direction; specifically the monetization read (dn move + spot-down-vol-down => fuel gone) and spot-up-vol-up during up moves.
4. $VIX9D / $VIX3M probe — do they serve via get_price_history_every_minute? If yes: fresh internals backup, add to SYMBOLS, force-backfill inside the rolling window, verify zero lost rows, and compute a term-structure trace ((VIX9D-VIX) 5-min change x (-dir)). If no: record the probe result and drop.
5. Re-score the convergence trio with the best VIX variant swapped in; report the new 0-3 table vs the original 25/49/65/73%.

Constraints: same honesty rules (day-clustered caveat, LOO fits, assert label-count parity 1,882 vs stored JSON before trusting results). Reuse morning_flush_continuation.py helpers; do not fork label parameters.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Dated section appended to docs/measurement/morning-flush-continuation.md with: de-seasoned vs raw AUC, beta fit (b, R^2) + residual AUC, quadrant table with n and P(CONT), probe outcome for both symbols stated, new convergence table
- Script committed under scripts/measurement/, re-runnable; label-parity assertion in code
- If term symbols serve: capture updated + backfill verified, st-3fr commented
- Re-rendered to /var/moo/desk; presented to Steve

title: Continuation trace — internals/VIX state that predicts flush continuation mid-move
description:
Steve's 2026-08-03 refinement after reading the contention review: less interested in statistical alignment (base rates, regime recency) than in a metric that bolsters confidence in CONTINUATION while the move is underway — Market Internals or VIX. The one-sided morning moves must leave a live trace beyond frequency.

## What is being built
Minute-level conditional study over the 22 July morning-move days (internals coverage begins 2026-06-18):
1. CONT/TERM labeling — for each minute inside a day's primary move (from morning_flush_study.json spans), outcome = new move-direction extreme within the next 15 min (minutes with truncated lookahead excluded).
2. Candidate traces at each minute, all causal/rolling, oriented so higher = confirms the move: $TICK level and 10-min sign-alignment share; $ADD and $VOLD 10-min slopes; $TRIN oriented level; ES cumulative-delta 5-min slope and delta-divergence flag; volume pace vs move average; wiggle-depth trend. VIX if backfill lands.
3. Separation ranking — per trace: median in CONT vs TERM populations, rank-sum P(cont>term) (AUC), and one swept threshold with hit/false-alarm counts. Honest n reporting; day-clustered caveat stated.
4. Backtest-event cut — at each resume_events T=2 event, trace state vs resumed/failed (n~476/21 — the actual re-entry decision point).
5. Day-level one-sidedness — TICK sign-share and VOLD magnitude vs move size (the "one-sided days leave a one-sided trace" check).

## VIX capture (same bead)
Schwab minute history is a rolling ~47-day window; internals corpus starts 06-18. If $VIX (or $VIX.X) serves via get_price_history_every_minute: add to SYMBOLS in scripts/corpus_pull_internals.py, back up data/corpus/*/internals.jsonl first, run --force backfill, verify no day lost rows and July days gained VIX. If the symbol does not serve, record that in the doc and drop VIX from scope.

## Non-obvious constraints
- Rewrite loop only touches days the API returns (rolled-off days safe) but a partial symbol failure during --force writes days missing that symbol — hence the backup + row-count verification.
- Internals are 1-min candles; ES tape is tick — align on minute boundaries, internals lag up to 59s. State it.
- climax-heat (st-u05, closed) measured confirm-heat, not continuation; cite, don't duplicate.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Morning flush anatomy + convergence signals (08:30-10:30 CT corpus study)
description:
Steve's 2026-08-03 directive (COO session, follow-on to Coded Counter Wisdom st-ug5): his contention is that the recent regime of large, often V-shaped moves inside the first 2 hours of the cash session is consistent enough to justify chasing the flush more vigorously than conventional wisdom accepts — enter, cut on the slightest backtest, re-enter if the flush resumes. Explicitly NOT drawdown tolerance: zero-tolerance cuts + liberal re-entry.

## What is being built
A corpus study over every day with morning ES tape (2026-07-03 onward, ~20 days, data/corpus/*/databento_glbx_es.jsonl 08:30-15:00 CT) restricted to the 08:30-10:30 CT window:
1. Morning-move census — per day: net move, max excursion, dominant leg (direction/size/duration/timing), V-shape flag (>=50% retrace of dominant leg inside window).
2. Flush anatomy — within each dominant leg: count/depth/duration of backtests at thresholds bracketing FD0's derived stop (~0.75/1.0/1.5/2.0 ES pts), resumption rate and time-to-new-extreme after each backtest.
3. Chase simulation — cut-on-backtest + re-enter-on-resumption vs one-and-done vs endure-drawdown, per day, in ES points captured net of per-attempt friction (FD0 friction model: spread+fees).
4. Convergence signals — covariates observable at/near entry time (gap vs prior close, first-5/15-min range/velocity/aggressor-delta from trades side field, $TICK from internals.jsonl, MBP-1 book imbalance, prior-day type, day of week) correlated against flush-day vs chop-day labels.

Reuses market/measurement/legprofiler.py bar/zigzag machinery and market/orderflow/replay.read_corpus_day. Read-only over the corpus; new script + analysis doc only.

## Non-obvious constraints
- n is ~20 days; report effect sizes honestly, no fitted thresholds presented as validated. Every numeric claim cited to its computation (no-confabulation standing rule).
- 2026-07-24 manifest says ES note 13:00-15:00 CT — verify actual coverage before including.
- FD0 (st-apzt) is NO-GO today; this is analysis, not a go signal.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Analysis doc committed at docs/measurement/morning-flush-anatomy.md with: per-day census table, backtest-anatomy distributions, chase-vs-baseline P&L table (friction-adjusted), and a candidate signal-convergence grading list ranked by observed separation, each with its false-positive count on the corpus.
- Script committed under scripts/measurement/ and re-runnable against future corpus days.
- Findings presented to Steve via rendered browser doc (shared-executable-space), not a file path.

All AC met. Doc committed (docs/measurement/morning-flush-anatomy.md, commit 3338a3d) with per-day census, anatomy distributions, friction-adjusted chase-vs-baseline table, and ranked convergence-signal list with false-positive counts; script re-runnable at scripts/measurement/morning_flush_study.py; delivered rendered to browser + desk NAV Reviews.

Headline: regime confirmed (median 52.6-pt primary move, 22/22 days; 16/22 start before 09:00). Backtests resume 96-98% (100% with >=5 pts remaining) — which indicts zero-tolerance cuts: every tight-stop chase variant net-negative at median even with oracle direction; oracle-direction endure +18.5/day median (20/22 days positive). Early tape ANTI-predicts direction (f5 net 8/22 agree; down-days gap up +13.2 and open +9.2); best graders: fade-f5>=4 (12/18), $TICK 09:00 sign (13/21), f15 volume for size (rho +0.57). title: Strader: pytest steals the Windows clipboard; make the payload push opt-in
description:
Steve hit this live on 2026-07-30: his clipboard held 'v1 2026-06-29 ES / S 5800 . minor key' instead of the day's 60-level payload.

Cause: tests/runbook/test_run.py calls run_mod.main(), which reaches run.py:473 payload_emitter.push_clipboard() -> real clip.exe via WSL interop. Nothing mocks it, so EVERY pytest run overwrites Steve's Windows clipboard with the _good_outcome() fixture (test_run.py:30-39 — date 2026-06-29, one support at 5800, no tier, cited in commentary, so it renders exactly the two lines he saw). Three pytest runs during the st-q1n cron work is what hit him.

The autouse _isolate_desk fixture at test_run.py:19-27 already guards DESK_REPORTS, DESK_REFRESH and DESK_HTML for precisely this reason — its own comment reads 'Without this a test run overwrites the browser page Steve keeps open. [st-lo2]'. The clipboard is the fourth surface in that set and the only unguarded one.

Second defect, same surface (Steve's call): the push fires on EVERY parse, so a diagnostic or backfill run seizes the clipboard too. It exists for the pre-open routine only (playbook: double-click indicator, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+V). Make it opt-in — off by default, --clip set explicitly by the 08:15 pre-open wrapper (st-q1n), so that cron is the only thing that ever loads the clipboard.

Fix: (1) repo-level tests/conftest.py autouse fixture stubbing push_clipboard so future test modules inherit the guard rather than re-discovering this; (2) --clip flag on run.py, default off.

title: TV/Mancini renderer rough edges — r-dropping bug, defense counter, label text editing
description:
Rough-edge pass on the stable Mancini renderer after Steve's first full days of live use (st-5rc closed 2026-07-28 on acceptance; these are the follow-ons).

## 1. Lowercase "r" is deleted from all label text (CRITICAL — renders notes illegible)

pine/mancini_forecast.pine line 69:
    lines = str.split(str.replace_all(payload, "\r", ""), "\n")

Intended to strip Windows-clipboard carriage returns. Pine does not read "\r"
as a carriage-return escape — it reads it as the literal character r — so
str.replace_all deletes EVERY lowercase r in the payload, including inside
words. Uppercase R survives (replace_all is case-sensitive), which is why the
" R" tier suffix looked fine.

Observed by Steve 2026-07-29: "rangebound" -> "angebound", "first" -> "fist",
"range" -> "ange". Confirmed against charts/2026-07-29.payload.txt, which has
all three spelled correctly on disk — the corruption is renderer-side only.

Fix: delete the replace_all. Line 72 already does str.trim() on each split
line, which strips a trailing CR; and note text is extracted from inside
quotes, so a CR past the closing quote never reaches it. No replacement
mechanism is needed.

## 2. The signed integer in labels is a bar count, not an event count

The "+88" Steve saw on 7483 is lvDefenses (pine line 227, incremented at line
134). It increments once per CONFIRMED BAR where the level is touched and
closes on the held side. On a 1-minute chart that counts minutes spent near
the level, so a level price hovers around all morning reads +88.

The intent was discrete approach-and-reject episodes. Fix: debounce — count a
defense on the transition into a touch episode, not on every bar within it.

## 3. Drop the S/R suffix from label text

Steve 2026-07-29: "You can drop the 'S' and 'R' - the color alone is enough."
pine line 225.

## 4. Label notes carry letter-summary prose instead of level-narrow facts

runbook/mancini/payload_emitter.py _note_for() takes the first sentence of the
first commentary anchored on the price, with no filter on what KIND of
commentary it is. Today's payload therefore ships:

  S 7434 "Positioning: Mancini is still holding a 10% long runner f..."
  R 7533 "Bull case: ES spends more time in the 7418-7506 range eng..."
  R 7548 "Bull case: ES spends more time in the 7418-7506 range eng..."  (dup)
  S 7418 "Regime: classic Mode 2 (rangebound) price action"

Steve 2026-07-29: "I never care what M. is holding. today's 7533 gives me Bull
Case: that info is for the letter summary, not labels. Reserve label text for
things very narrow to that level like 'tested multiple times' or 'strong'."

Also note the mid-word truncation ("runner f...", "eng...") — a symptom of
forcing 60 chars of narrative into a label rather than selecting a short fact.

Fix is emitter-side: admit only level-narrow descriptors; reject positioning /
bull-case / bear-case / regime commentary; de-duplicate identical notes across
levels.

## 5. Unidentified panel, upper-right, containing "to"

Steve wants it gone. Not yet identified — the renderer's HUD defaults to
top_left and has no "to" cell. Could be the HUD relocated via the "HUD
position" input, or one of the three LuxAlgo indicators sharing the /ES tab.
Needs Steve to identify before action.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Payload text renders with lowercase r intact; a regression test asserts a
  note containing "rangebound"/"first" survives the parse path.
- Defense counter reflects discrete touch episodes; unit test with synthetic
  bars proves N bars inside one episode yields +1, not +N.
- Labels carry no S/R suffix.
- No label text contains positioning, bull-case, bear-case, or regime prose;
  emitter unit test covers the rejection; no two levels carry the same note.
- Upper-right panel identified and removed or explained.
- Steve confirms on a live TradingView chart.
close_reason: All six rough edges resolved and confirmed live by Steve. r-dropping traced to Pine reading "\r" as the literal character r in str.replace_all, deleting every lowercase r in the payload. Defense counter debounced to touch episodes. S/R suffix dropped. Label notes now short level-quality descriptors from a fixed vocabulary, letter-summary commentary rejected. Upper-right panel was a stale TV artifact, cleared by restart. Label backgrounds default to chart.bg_color. Commits ed4528e, acf2168.

title: task
description:
Found at tap-in 2026-07-25 (Sat 06:46 CT). PID 177811 launched Fri 7/24 09:12 CT by the gauge-preopen cron wrapper is STILL running 21h34m later, appending one row per minute into data/corpus/2026-07-24/mi_gauge_live.jsonl. Latest row: 2026-07-25T06:46 close=-490 on a closed market.

Two defects:
1. No session-close exit. Cron (*/5 8-15 * * 1-5) only launches/respawns; the process itself has no stop condition, so it runs through the close, overnight, and into the weekend.
2. No day rollover. The capture day is fixed at launch, so Saturday rows land in Friday's file.

Impact: ~1000 of 1367 rows in the 7/24 capture are post-close garbage. This is the forward-capture sample st-3fr calibration depends on — the sample needs to be trimmed to RTH before it is used.

Fix: exit at a configured session end (default 15:15 CT), guard writes against a day mismatch, and have the cron wrapper treat 'not running outside session hours' as correct rather than respawn-worthy. Backfill: trim the 7/24 file to RTH.

Recommended immediate action (Steve's call): kill 177811.
close_reason: Gauge self-exits at STRADER_GAUGE_SESSION_END (default 15:15 CT) and on day rollover, both evaluated before create_client() and re-checked each tick; append_capture refuses foreign-day writes. Wrapper no longer respawns outside 08:00-15:15 CT Mon-Fri and WARNs (never kills) a survivor. Backfill: 7/24 capture 1712 -> 435 rows, raw preserved as mi_gauge_live.raw.jsonl, replay parity confirmed (390m, cum -71). PID 177811 killed by Steve 2026-07-25 13:07 CT, file re-trimmed. remain-on-exit switched to 'failed' per Steve. 22 new tests. Commit 5cee846.

title: Strader2 Phase 3: singleton entity model (0DTE long single as futures proxy)
description:
## Context
Phase 3 of Strader2 (plan co-r10h; scope st-nd5). The first genuinely new strategy code: the single-leg entity. None exists — market/entities/Position wraps ButterflyInstance only.

## Design
Mirror the frozen-dataclass conventions in market/entities/. Two entities in strader2/entities/singleton.py:
- SingletonSetup: the trade idea — bias (bullish/bearish → long call/put), Carmine trigger (failed_breakdown/level_reclaim/return_to_lvn/range_trap, recognized from datafeed per §6.2), anchor Level (the reference frame), mancini_confluence flag (highest conviction when a Carmine zone coincides with a Mancini level).
- SingletonPosition: an entered single-leg long option framed as a futures proxy ('a single is a futures contract on its last day'). Carries the Contract leg, setup, entry/current premium, underlying at entry + now, target/stop (underlying points). Futures-proxy lenses: net_delta, delta_exposure ($/pt), unrealized_pnl, max_loss (= premium, long-option defined risk), r_multiple, pts_to_target/stop, at_target/at_stop. Delta is the litmus, not theta.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] strader2/entities/singleton.py with SingletonSetup + SingletonPosition (frozen dataclasses, matching market/entities style).
- [ ] Consistency guard: bullish→CALL, bearish→PUT (reject mismatch).
- [ ] Unit tests: right-mapping, delta sign, exposure, pnl, max_loss, r_multiple, target/stop distances for both biases.
- [ ] Does NOT automate orders; entity/data only (evaluator + recognition are Phase 4).
close_reason: Singleton entity built + tested. strader2/entities/singleton.py: SingletonSetup + SingletonPosition (frozen, matches market/entities). Futures-proxy lenses (net_delta/delta_exposure/r_multiple/at_target/at_stop), bias<->right guard. 9 unit tests, full suite 31 green. Commit pushed to master. Data-only; recognition + evaluator are Phase 4.

title: Strader2 Phase 2: fix Mancini empty-levels[] extraction (co-y2hg)
description:
## Symptom
The Mancini LLM parser (runbook/mancini/llm.py) fills session_bias but returns levels:[] and commentary:[] (confirmed: parsed/2026-06-29.json has 0 levels, 0 commentary, session_bias populated). COO bead co-y2hg.

## Root cause
NOT a schema or content problem. Letters are dense with explicit levels ('Supports are: 7383, 7377 (major), ...' ~27; 'Resistances are: ...' ~30; plus Bull/Bear/Summary forward guidance). The SYSTEM_PROMPT is over-conservative — 'if unsure, omit', 'downstream rejects any price not found verbatim, so do not guess' — pushing the model to return empty rather than risk rejection. 'required' on the array only forces the key to exist; [] satisfies it.

## Fix
Rewrite SYSTEM_PROMPT to be extraction-POSITIVE: name where levels live (the explicit Supports/Resistances lists + inline Bull/Bear/Summary targets/pivots), state that empty levels for a normal letter is an error, keep verbatim-accuracy as a correctness rule (not a reason to omit), allow minimal verbatim source_quote spans. Bump MAX_TOKENS for level-dense letters.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One paid live extraction on a cached dense letter (mancini/archive/2026-05-19) returns many levels (>=20) + commentary (>=3), all prices verbatim (validation passes).
- [ ] Existing mancini unit tests still green (they mock extract).
- [ ] co-y2hg unblocked; runbook pilot close (co-7lyf) can proceed.
close_reason: Fixed + paid-verified. Prompt rewritten extraction-positive; MAX_TOKENS->16000. Live run on 2026-05-19 cached letter: 61 levels + 6 commentary, validation.ok=True (was 0/0). 31 unit tests green. Commit pushed to master. Unblocks runbook pilot close co-7lyf.

title: V-drop-and-recovery detection + greek correlation in late-day window (corpus measurement)
description:
Steve directed 2026-05-23 evening: isolate the late-day vega/convexity drop and recovery pattern, correlate the greeks (gamma, vanna, charm) during that process. This is the operational measurement work that the OPRA + ES backfill enables.

## The pattern (from existing doctrine)

The 2025-07-25 jass canonical entry (principal_discord.md) documents the three-phase pattern:
1. Lift convexity (morning) — customer convexity buying
2. Dump (~12:00-12:30 ET) — aggressive sell-off of long convexity
3. Ramp (post-dump) — directional move, dealer hedging flips from short-stock-vs-customer-long to long-stock-vs-customer-short

jass's operational rule: 'those are the best longs tho. there's juice to lean on.'

## What we'll measure

For each trading day in the late-day window (13:00-15:00 CT = 14:00-16:00 ET):
1. Compute a 'V' series — likely net convexity from OPRA option trades, or net vega aggregate. Need to pick the canonical V metric.
2. Detect drop events — sharp downward moves in V within a ≤30-min window, configurable threshold.
3. Detect recovery — V returns toward starting level (or price ramps in the expected direction) within the remaining session.
4. For each detected event, snapshot the greek profile at: pre-drop, mid-drop, post-drop, post-ramp. Look for systematic patterns in how gamma/vanna/charm shift.

## What we'll need

- OPRA SPXW trades for the window — IN PROGRESS via st-xc9 (currently ~162/250 days done, walking back to 2025-05-24)
- ES price series for the window — QUEUED via the chain script (kicks in when OPRA backfill finishes)
- Black-Scholes greek calculator — exists somewhere in Strader codebase or in the gex-llm-patterns reference (src/gex/ has BS implementation; license-compatible, may be cleaner to write our own based on standard formulas)
- A canonical V metric definition — needs decision (net convexity? net vega? something derived?)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Definition document for 'V drop' (threshold, window length, scope) committed to docs/measurement/
- Detection script that emits one row per detected event with timestamp + magnitude + recovery outcome
- Greek-snapshot script that, given a detected event, produces the pre/mid/post-drop/post-ramp greek profiles
- First-pass report: how many V-drop events in the backfilled year, base-rate recovery, greek-shift summary statistics
- Cross-reference back to the 2025-07-25 jass canonical entry — does the data corroborate jass's three-phase narrative?

## Dependencies

- Blocked on st-xc9 backfill completion (both OPRA and ES legs)
- Possibly waiting on a decision about the canonical V metric — surface for Steve when planning detection script

title: Add Jasper 2025-09-29 + 2025-10-01 canonical entry — GEX vs gamma definitions, Classic vs State product distinction
description:
Steve flagged 2026-05-23: two Jasper Discord threads, sequential dates, same evolving doctrine. Worth a single combined canonical entry.

## Thread 1 (2025-09-29 9:41-10:29 PM): GEX vs gamma definitions

pensivelion [end] (community): 'what's the difference between GEX being positive and gamma being positive?'

Jasper (9:45 PM): canonical definitions
- GEX profile = netting CALL vs PUT gamma (irrespective of long/short initiator)
- Gamma profile (under options profile) = netting LONG vs SHORT gamma (irrespective of call/put)
- Practically: GEX = net long/short DELTAS at strike (calls/puts are the dimension); gamma = net long/short VOL (straddles — whether customer lifted or dumped vol at strike)
- The original GEX assumption was 'customers always long puts, short calls' → dealer short puts, long calls — 'useless for 0dte/intraday' → actual classification via vol surface necessary

Jasper (10:29 PM): vol surface normalization aside
- Why convert prices to volatilities: $0.02 OTM call vs $0.50 ATM call can't be price-compared directly (moneyness mismatch)
- Recommends Investopedia for deeper read

## Thread 2 (2025-10-01 1:02-1:08 PM): Classic vs State product distinction (CONTINUES from 9/29)

Browniver [PHUB] (community): 'difference in GEX profile in classic and state is volatility surface classification? What does it mean for real life trading? What to use?'

Jasper (1:05 PM):
- Classic: 'naively incrementing volume of each option contract as it trades, and then incorporates that into the gamma exposure calculation' — the naive vendor approach
- State: 'classifies the trades of the option contract as buy or sell (so the volume can be +50 which means 50 lots bot, or -25 which means 25 lots sold, all cumulatively over the day) before then calculating gex exposure with that'
- 'you'll see in a lot of literature the naive assumption of paper buys puts and sells calls, therefore dealer is short puts and long calls, but that assumption is clearly just wrong'

Jasper (1:08 PM): operational implications
- State enables vol-regime reads: all long vol → 'hotter tape'; all short vol → 'join the grind'
- For level-to-level scalping: 'state just better indicates where shorts or longs are located on the profile'
- 'classic (naive) gex profile generally fills out calls to the upside, puts to the downside' (the naive assumption shows directly in chart shape)

## Doctrinal payload

1. Canonical GEX vs gamma definitions (axes: GEX = call/put net = directional; gamma = long/short net = vol)
2. Repudiation of the naive 'paper buys puts, sells calls' assumption
3. Product distinction: Classic = naive volume-increment GEX; State = trade-classified signed-volume GEX
4. Regime trading via State: long-vol regime = active tape; short-vol regime = grind/pass
5. Vol surface normalization rationale (moneyness-comparable values)

title: Add Jasper 2025-09-28 vqz canonical entry — two-signal fade-entry rule (long gamma + directional GEX)
description:

## The exchange

vqz [MATH] (community), 12:53 PM: asks if his read is correct — fade ES means looking for long gamma spike + GEX spike upside.

Jasper (Moderator), 2:49 PM:
- 'yes. if you're looking to bid for reversion against spot selling off, the ideal conditions are long gamma + downside (put) gex spiking. this means someone's stepping in for reversion and making downside expensive. so spot price goes up'
- 'conversely long gamma + upside (call) gex -> short'

## Doctrinal payload

The two-signal fade-entry rule:
- Long gamma spike + downside (put) GEX spiking → bid for reversion (LONG entry)
- Long gamma spike + upside (call) GEX spiking → SHORT entry

Mechanism: 'making it expensive = stepping in for reversion.' Put GEX spike on downside = customers buying puts = paying premium against downside = expecting reversion UP. The dealer hedging of the long puts provides the buy pressure.

This sharpens the canonical pivot-at-long-gamma rule by adding direction: net gamma identifies the LEVEL; directional GEX identifies the TRADE DIRECTION at that level.

title: John Kirby Discord 2025-05-14/15 — Izzy Q&A, double-warning + Bullish-Above-Bearish-Below patterns
description:
Substantial principal Q&A exchange. Izzy (community) raises good conceptual questions about the gamma filter losing put/call composition information. yungissh (community) chimes in trying to understand the same thing. John M (John Kirby) responds with a worked example from 2025-05-14 + a reference to a similar pattern from 2025-05-13. Three graphics attached.

Q (Izzy, 2025-05-14 5:43 PM):
1. Doesn't the gamma filter cause you to miss put/call composition?
2. For an accelerant, don't you want trapped short put sellers (price falling) or short call sellers (price rising)?
3. What's the "perfect trade setup"? Wouldn't it be large long gamma node + short gamma PUSHING price toward it, where the put-vs-call composition of the surrounding short gamma matters?

Q (yungissh, 5/14 7:31 PM): same kind of question — trying to understand the gamma filter; observes price gets attracted to largest gamma clusters; once first wall is reached, either breaks-and-fails or mellows between two largest nodes.

A (John, 2025-05-15 6:07 AM, 6:20 AM, 6:35 AM): three-part walkthrough.

A1 (6:07 AM): Workflow rule. "Once market opens and settles in after 15-20 minutes, capture a screenshot for yourself to mark up." On 5/14 he immediately marked Calls Sold + Puts Bought at ES $5919 = "DOUBLE WARNING" for bearish morning. Calls Sold position grew to >2000 contracts. Then toggle to Gamma view for confirmation. (Graphic izzy2)

A2 (6:20 AM): Hypothetical mechanics. ES at $5890, Calls Bought at $5910 = positive gamma. If no larger negative gamma overtakes, cyan blue extends right (= net long gamma). Price rising to meet Calls Bought at $5910 → "expect some initial profit taking" → this is the theory behind the positive gamma level as "initial Point of Reversion" — profit taking prevents further upside unless order flow is extremely bullish.

A3 (6:35 AM): The Bullish-Above/Bearish-Below pattern (graphic izzy3 from 5/13). Calls Bought + Puts Bought at SAME price level = "Bullish Above/Bearish Below" pivot. ES $5920 was the battle line on 5/13 → became the resistance problem at $5919/$5920 on 5/14. Also works for Calls Sold + Puts Sold at same level (the inverse).

Net new content:
1. "Double warning" pattern: Calls Sold + Puts Bought at same level = bearish wall
2. "Bullish Above/Bearish Below" pattern: Calls Bought + Puts Bought at same level (or Calls Sold + Puts Sold) = pivot in either direction
3. "Initial Point of Reversion" mechanism: positive gamma stalls via profit-taking at the level, not just MM hedging
4. Cross-day persistence: gamma walls from prior session can carry over (5/13 → 5/14)
5. Workflow discipline: 15-20 min post-open screenshot for markup → identify levels → toggle to gamma view for confirmation
6. Implicit answer to Izzy: use BOTH views (Options for composition + Gamma for net polarity); don't choose one

title: John Kirby Discord 2025-04-04 — when gamma stops failing in put-dominated regime
description:
Principal Q&A. stockholm (community) asks John Kirby about a case where negative gamma levels DON'T act as expected stops. Date 2025-04-04, 11:21 AM → 12:39 PM.

This is important because it documents a FAILURE MODE of the gamma-pivots rule — sustained selling can overwhelm gamma-based supports.

stockholm Q1: "negative gamma levels dont seem to be stopping the move. Why is that?"
John A1: "Selling Calls and Selling Puts creates Negative Gamma. It also dumps more liquidity into the markets pushing the market lower. We are also in a 'Put' dominated environment."

stockholm Q2 (correct mechanical observation): "short puts and long puts are counteracting forces from a delta hedging perspective. Long puts will create selling pressure where as short puts will create buying pressure. Im not following why the DEX from short puts is not acting as a stop for the falling markets"

John A2: "Until some sort of positive news flow enters the market to establish short covering and call buying, 'Dealers' have to keep selling futures while they are below specific Gamma levels. Their selling is completely outweighing any of the options positions. Did you happen to take note of the 'Put Selling' above spot price this morning. There were quite a few attempts where they sold Puts pricing 70% volatility. I would gather that these Put Sales were just hedges for the pounding they were doing on futures."

John A3 (worked example): "They came in and sold a few thousand of the ES $5237.00 Puts at 9:50 am. and by 10:15 they smashed right through them. Those key concepts regarding gamma are from Freddie's YouTube class. https://www.youtube.com/@gextrading"

1. **Sustained selling can overwhelm gamma levels** — even short-put-driven buy-support fails under regime stress
2. **Put-selling-above-spot as a HEDGE** — institutions selling puts at 70% IV above spot as cover for the larger short futures position. The put sale isn't the bet, it's the hedge.
3. **Regime context matters**: "put dominated environment" creates conditions where normal gamma rules suspend
4. **Specific failed example**: ES $5237 puts sold few thousand at 9:50 AM → smashed through by 10:15

title: Three-stream corpus: Schwab + GexBot + Databento OPRA
description:
## Goal

Stand up per-day, append-only ledger of three independent market data streams so we can read the late-day 0DTE gamma/charm footprints across many sessions. Building the corpus is the prerequisite for any model-mastery work — without a multi-day record, we cannot validate (or falsify) GexBot's classification against raw OPRA tape.

## Streams

1. **Schwab session record** — spot SPX + /ES quotes, 0DTE ATM chain (±10 strikes) snapshot, ATM straddle, ATM IV. 5-min cadence during cash hours (8:30-15:00 CT). Free (entitlement via brokerage).

2. **GexBot State** — `/SPX/state/{gamma,vanna,charm,delta}_zero` plus `/SPX/classic/gex_zero/majors` (the only majors endpoint that works for our tier per the st-rks probe). 5-min cadence. Flat $150/mo.

3. **Databento OPRA option ticks** — all SPXW (incl 0DTE) trades for the late-day window (13:00-15:00 CT initially). Historical batch pull, T+1, dataset=`OPRA.PILLAR`, schema=`trades`, symbols=["SPXW.OPT"], stype_in=`parent`. ~$6-8 per session per get_cost probe (verified entitled 2026-05-22).

## Storage

Per-day directory `data/corpus/YYYY-MM-DD/`:
- `schwab.jsonl` — append, one row per intraday cycle
- `gexbot.jsonl` — append, one row per intraday cycle, all 5 endpoint responses bundled
- `databento_opra.jsonl` — written once per day by T+1 batch
- `manifest.json` — what was collected, when, errors

JSONL = append-only, easy to inspect with jq, cheap incremental reads. `data/corpus/` gitignored (corpus grows large).

## Scripts

- `scripts/corpus_pull_schwab.py` — one cycle, idempotent, writes one JSONL line
- `scripts/corpus_pull_gexbot.py` — one cycle, all 5 endpoints, writes one line
- `scripts/corpus_pull_databento.py` — batch pull for a given date (run T+1)
- `scripts/corpus_poll.py` — orchestrator: runs Schwab + GexBot together; loop with --max-runs / --interval

## Acceptance Criteria

- All four scripts compile and run end-to-end smoke against live APIs
- One Schwab cycle, one GexBot cycle, and one Databento batch (yesterday 2026-05-21 SPXW late-day) all produce well-formed JSONL with timestamps and full provenance
- Data field provenance: every value cites its source endpoint and the response timestamp it came from
- `data/corpus/` is gitignored
- No interpretive labels (no "regime", no "pinning") in the raw stream — those are derivations for later
- ~/.schwab_gate_key check honored for the Schwab stream
- Databento cost stays in the $6-8/session range for the chosen window

## Why P1

Steve flagged 2026-05-22 that the framework can't progress without a corpus. Every "vet read" attempt I've made has been ungrounded interpretive content because I don't have multi-day pattern data to anchor on. The corpus IS the substrate. Until it exists, my opinions on a given day's late-day move aren't reliably worth more than noise. Parent bead: st-rks (which scoped Layer 4 measurement; this expands and supersedes that layer's design).
close_reason:
Corpus stood up end-to-end in commit e1913b2. All three streams landed:

(1) Schwab + GexBot polling (intraday): one-cycle scripts plus orchestrator. Verified 2026-05-22 pre-open: 1 Schwab row (SPX 7445.72, ATM K 7445), 1 GexBot row (5 endpoints bundled, gamma_zero spot 7445.29, mpos 7450 / mneg 7445 / mLg 7439.80 / mSg 7449.68). Both clean, no errors.

(2) Databento OPRA batch (T+2): historical pull verified on 2026-05-18 13:00-13:05 CT validation window — 21,198 SPXW ticks with full OSI symbology (e.g., SPXW  260518P07395000) at $0.50.

Two operational findings logged in commit:
- Databento OPRA historical embargo: data after [yesterday market open] requires Live license. Effective limit: T+2 batch from today, T+1 if pulled before market open. Documented; not blocking for corpus purposes (learning, not trading intraday).
- Symbology requires to_df() not raw iteration. First-attempt pull 2026-05-20 (349k ticks, $4.37) had null symbols; bug caught and corrected on validation pull. 5/20 file retained on disk with intact prices/sizes/instrument_ids/timestamps but per-strike attribution would need a symbology backfill if revived.

Total spend: ~$5 ($4.37 broken first pull + $0.50 validation pull on the corrected code). Going-forward cadence: ~$5-8 per session at the 2-hour late-day window.

AC met: (a) all 4 scripts compile + run end-to-end smoke against live APIs ✓, (b) JSONL well-formed with full provenance ✓, (c) data/corpus/ gitignored via top-level data/ ✓, (d) no interpretive labels (regime, pinning) in raw stream ✓, (e) Schwab gate honored ✓, (f) Databento spend in target range ✓.

Next step for the corpus is to actually run it: corpus_poll.py on a 5-min cron during cash hours (8:30-15:00 CT) plus corpus_pull_databento.py invoked T+2 each morning for the prior session's late-day window. Pattern study comes after ~5-10 days accumulate.

title: Orderflow sentinel — coded level-proximity watcher that summons the x-ray read
description:
## What
Steve's 2026-08-10 directive: COO functions as a real-life trader during live sessions — same instruments and views Steve uses — with a tiered team: deterministic code watches, Fable performs the deep read ('x-ray') at decision points. This bead is the watcher.

## Shape (v1, shipped today)

- spot entering a proximity band (default 2.5 SPX pts) around z_mlgamma / z_msgamma while approaching; re-arms when distance exceeds 5 pts

Alerts append to data/corpus/<date>/orderflow_alerts.jsonl and render in tmux steves-desk:sentinel. COO watches the alerts file (harness Monitor) and delivers the x-ray read on each wake: spike train around the trigger, aggdex quadrant, net-convexity trend, verdict in doctrine terms.

## v2 (not this bead's AC, tracked here for continuity)
- Convexity-dump detector (jass dump-then-ramp: >50% collapse from morning peak inside 30 min)
- Supervision parity (cron wrapper like the collectors); heartbeat
- GEX-OF spike-threshold trigger once Phase 2 sizes 'meaningful vs prior spikes'

## Acceptance Criteria
- With the 1 Hz leg live, an approach to within the band produces exactly one alert (no spam), visible in the tmux window and the alerts file.
- Level relocation produces an alert naming old/new values.
- Sentinel survives file rollover to the next day path and idles harmlessly off-session.

title: Live 1 Hz orderflow leg — dedicated poller for /SPX/orderflow/orderflow
description:
## What
A dedicated session-gated poller for the single orderflow endpoint at ~1.1s spacing — the vendor's stated ceiling is 'one request per second per ticker per metric' (AGENTS.md, quoted in docs/gexbot/vendor-docs-survey-2026-08-06.md §Cadence). The main 10-endpoint collector stays at 60s; this leg exists because Steve's 2026-08-10 steer makes REAL-TIME direction reads the target, and a 70s sample cannot see spike trains (the whole content of the gex/convexity orderflow panes). Nightly /hist covers 1s data retrospectively; this closes the live gap.

## Shape
- scripts/corpus_poll_gexbot_orderflow_1s.py — same session gate as corpus_poll_gexbot.py (08:30–15:05 CT, holiday-aware), persistent HTTP client, dedup on identical consecutive payloads, entitlement-lapse backoff (Sep 1 downgrade must not spin at 1s), writes flat rows to data/corpus/<date>/gexbot_orderflow_1s.jsonl, manifest stream gexbot_orderflow_1s batched every 60 polls.

- Kill the process mid-session: supervisor relaunches within 2 min; manifest cycles advance.
- Outside the window / on holidays it exits without polling.
- Entitlement lapse (401/403 or error body) backs off to 5 min, no spin.
- Test run with --max-cycles writes the expected rows.

title: Nightly gexbot hist harvest leaves Friday unharvested until Monday 21:00
description:
## Problem
scripts/gexbot_hist_nightly.sh runs via cron '0 21 * * 1-5' and calls gexbot_hist_backfill.py --days 3, whose lookback excludes the run day itself. Observed in /var/moo/logs/gexbot-hist-nightly.log: the Friday 2026-08-07 21:00 run processed only 08-04/05/06. With no Sat/Sun cron, Friday's session history cannot land before Monday 21:00 — during Monday's trading day the freshest 1s history is Thursday's. Found 2026-08-10 when the 08-07 day-dir was absent from data/corpus/gexbot-hist/.

## Fix
Include the run day in the nightly lookback (the 21:00 slot is 3h post-close, /hist is complete by then — verify once), or add a weekend catch-up run. Keep --days >= 3 so missed nights self-heal.

## Steps to Reproduce
grep '2026-08-07T21' -A4 /var/moo/logs/gexbot-hist-nightly.log — the run covers 08-04..06 only; ls data/corpus/gexbot-hist/ lacks 2026-08-07.

## Acceptance Criteria
- After a Friday 21:00 run, data/corpus/gexbot-hist/<friday>/ exists with the standard file set and manifest rows.
- A skipped night still self-heals on the next run.
- One log line states the date range the run covered.

title: Strader: datastream gate reads live-capture last_pull as freshness — fails every Monday
description:
The gate halts on data-day 2026-08-07 with "stream 'databento_glbx_es' is stale: last pull 64.2h ago (> 36.0h)", blocking the 2026-08-10 Mancini parse. The 06:30 corpus_daily run had already hit it and exited rc=1 at 06:32 with the same reason.

MECHANISM. runbook/datastream/gate.py checks each required stream's manifest last_pull_utc against DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_HOURS = 36.0. For a stream filled by the T+1 batch, last_pull_utc is the FETCH time, so it refreshes every morning. For a stream filled by LIVE capture it is the SESSION END — 2026-08-07T20:05:00Z, Friday 15:05 CT — and nothing touches it again, because corpus_daily has nothing to fetch for a stream live capture already populated. Friday close to Monday 07:15 CT is 64.2h, so this now fails every Monday by construction. The comment on the constant literally reads 'T+1 batch + weekend slack'; the slack does not cover it.

WHY IT DID NOT FIRE BEFORE. 2026-07-31's manifest has databento_glbx_es last_pull 2026-08-03T11:31:05Z — the Monday T+1 batch DID re-pull ES for that Friday, so the gate saw a 1.7h-old stream and passed. 2026-08-06 and 2026-08-07 both show last_pull equal to the live stream end instead. Something changed in whether the batch re-pulls ES between 07-31 and 08-06; the 2026-08-05 capture-window ruling (st-btu) is the obvious suspect but is UNVERIFIED.

THE DATA IS FINE. 2026-08-07 landed 377,721 ES ticks / 151.7 MB with a clean 'live stream ended — 0 reconnect(s)' note. Today's live capture is UP (4h11m at 07:19 CT). This is a freshness-metric defect, not missing data — which is the dangerous kind, because the fix everyone reaches for is --no-gate.

FIX DIRECTION (not decided): the gate should measure the age of the DATA, not the age of the last write. Candidates: (a) compare last_pull_utc to the data-day's own session close rather than to now; (b) have live capture stamp a separate completed_utc the gate reads; (c) make max_age relative to trading days elapsed rather than wall-clock hours. Do NOT just raise 36 to 72 — that blinds the gate to a genuinely dead Friday feed, which is the failure it exists to catch. Precedent: on 2026-08-07 the same shape was fixed by removing databento_opra from DEFAULT_REQUIRED_STREAMS rather than by adding a bypass, on the rule that a gate which fails every morning trains its operator to bypass it.
close_reason:
Fixed 2026-08-10, commit ed25f75. The gate now asks whether a stream COVERS its data-day (last write at or after that day's session close, less 10 min slack) instead of whether it was written recently. Early-close aware via strader.market_calendar, so a 12:00 CT half session is judged against noon. max_age_hours retained only as the fallback for a manifest with no usable date. checked[stream] now carries covers_day.

Verified: the real 2026-08-07 manifest passes at 69h old with covers_day=True, and scripts/cron/mancini-preopen-wrapper.sh runs rc=0 end to end. 974 tests pass, with fixtures rewritten to anchor on a CT clock time on the data-day — an age-anchored fixture cannot express 'healthy Friday read on Monday morning', which is the case that used to fail.

Rejected: --no-gate at the call site (trains the operator to bypass, per Steve's 2026-08-07 ruling on the same shape for OPRA) and raising 36h to 72h (buys one weekend, blinds the check to a Friday feed that died at 10:00).

ERRATUM: I cited this bead as 'st-jc8p' in the commit message, in CurrentStatus.md and in conversation. The real ID is st-1qpz. CurrentStatus corrected; the commit message is pushed and stands wrong.

title: Strader: EOD Ritual — close the trading day, not just the session
description: Steve 2026-08-09: sessions are permitted to span one day to the next, and the current rituals are not aligned with that. Diagnosis: DaysActivity.md is created lazily by /handoff and rolled lazily by /tap-in, so nothing is anchored to the day itself. On 2026-08-08 five commits landed with no handoff and the day got no record at all — the substantive finding (round-4 scalp metrics, two-signal retired for the singleton lane) survived only in a commit message. Design (Strader-local; the enterprise DaysActivity convention is COO's and is NOT being changed): /handoff stays the SESSION record. A new /eod is the TRADING-DAY record — the thing only Strader has. Following the precedent Steve set for /mancini-parse (cron prepares and alerts; the skill owns the interpretation), a 15:15 CT cron gathers the day's facts into a durable packet at data/eod/<date>.md and the /eod skill reads it and writes a Day Close entry. That way the facts are captured mechanically and cannot be lost, the narrative stays agent-written at the right moment, and a day with a packet but no Day Close entry is a VISIBLE gap surfaced at tap-in rather than a silent one.

comments.author: Steve
comments.text:
Built and installed 2026-08-09 (commit f9e299c). Design decisions worth keeping:

(1) The enterprise DaysActivity convention is NOT changed. /eod adds an entry type; /handoff, /tap-in's roll, and the archive step are untouched. DaysActivity.md exists in 9+ repos and its format is COO's authority — but a TRADING DAY is a thing only Strader has, which is what justifies a Strader-only sibling ritual rather than a restructure.

(2) The packet is durable on disk BEFORE any agent reads it. The failure being fixed is a day whose facts evaporated because nobody was at the desk; a packet that only exists inside a session that may never happen reproduces the bug.

(3) Only HARD gaps alert — a stream at 0 cycles (tape unrecoverable) or GEX rows outside the collect window (gate breach). Soft gaps (ungraded call, missing Mancini entry) are for /eod to notice. An alert that fires most days is not an alert.

(4) RITUAL_START = 2026-08-10 so --audit does not report every trading day in repo history as a gap.

REMAINING before close: the ritual has not run once. First real fire is Monday 2026-08-10 15:15 CT; first /eod is Steve's or mine after that. Close when one full cycle has produced a Day Close entry that --audit accepts.

title: Strader: Pine lvState RECLAIMED has no outgoing transition — 'rcl' is sticky for the session
description: In the Pine level indicator, lvState 3 (RECLAIMED) has no transition out, so once a level is reclaimed the 'rcl' label persists for the rest of the session even after price breaks the level again. Pairs with asymmetric hysteresis: a break requires a 2-point buffer, a reclaim requires none. Both must be fixed together or the label oscillates on every touch. title: Strader: RTH-gate the gexbot poller — it runs 24/7 and logged 58 MB on a closed Saturday
description: scripts/corpus_poll_gexbot.py is a bare --interval 60 loop with no session gate. Observed: 2026-08-07 (Fri) wrote gexbot.jsonl until 23:59 CT; 2026-08-08 (Sat, market closed) wrote 58.4 MB / ~1153 cycles across the full day; 2026-08-09 (Sun) wrote 3.7 MB until 01:30 CT, when the process died on its own (not running as of 13:58 CT Sunday). CurrentStatus.md claims 'Feed is RTH-only — collector DOWN outside 08:30-15:00 CT is normal', which the data contradicts. Fix: add a session gate to the poll loop (sleep-until-open outside 08:30-15:00 CT weekdays, honoring the market holiday calendar) OR drop the RTH-only claim from CurrentStatus.md. Both cannot stand. Secondary: find out why the process exited at 01:30 Sunday and whether it is supervised at all.

comments.author: Steve
comments.text: 2026-08-10: the gate (commit f6b8b20) was REVERTED at Steve's direction. scripts/corpus_poll_gexbot.py is once again a bare --interval 60 loop with no session gate, so this defect is LIVE, not fixed. The measurement stands: 2026-08-08 (Sat, market closed) 1153 cycles / 58.4 MB; 2026-08-07 wrote through 23:59 CT. CurrentStatus.md again carries the unenforced 'RTH-only' claim.

comments.author: Steve
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-10 (Steve caught it, commit 36f0a81). This bead's framing was partly wrong and the wrong part was the part I asserted rather than measured.

CurrentStatus.md's 'Feed is RTH-only — collector DOWN outside 08:30-15:00 CT is normal' is a statement about the VENDOR'S DATA and it is TRUE. I read it as a claim about the collector process, tested it against process behaviour, and called it 'measured false'. Category error. The collector being ungated and the feed being RTH-only are both true and are different facts.

Measured from 2026-08-07's own capture: spot_at_gamma_zero frozen at ONE value 00:00-08:29 CT, first new value 08:30:02, ~76s cadence to 15:00:33, flat after. Saturday 2026-08-08: 1153 polls, ONE distinct value all day.

Consequences fixed: collect window 07:30 -> 08:30 (the 'pre-open ramp' comment asserted the opposite of the truth and would have written ~60 duplicate rows every morning); CurrentStatus restored to the true claim with the measurement behind it; consumer warning restated — pre-gate files are ~70% VERBATIM REPEATS, not stale-but-plausible data, so they must be deduplicated before any count/average/weight.

Withdrawn: the quota argument. I never verified that GexBot's QUANT tier meters requests and should not have asserted it. The surviving justification for the gate is narrower and sufficient: it stops writing ~1,100 duplicate rows a day into the corpus.

title: Round 4 — scalp-metric re-score: MFE/MAE and fast-move tails for orderflow signals
description:

title: Strader: sweep emission says 'ticks' where it means price levels — UI + field name
description: SweepPrint.ticks_swept is a COUNT OF DISTINCT PRICE LEVELS (engine.py:_end_run: ticks = len(r['prices'])), not ticks of travel. The engine's own reason string is correct ('3 levels, 310 contracts') but orderflow_drill_template.html emGist() rendered it as 'through 3 ticks', which reads as distance and confused Steve on the 8/07 close (bar 488, 14:59:58). A 3-level walk 7778.00->7778.50 is 2 ticks of travel. Display fixed to 'levels' 2026-08-08. Remaining: the field name ticks_swept is itself the trap — rename to levels_swept across market/signals/orderflow.py, engine.py, tests and the parity snapshot, or document it loudly. Also worth revisiting whether 'sweep' is the right word at all: SWEEP_MIN_TICKS=3 means every minimum sweep scores exactly confidence 0.50 (min(1.0, ticks/6)), so 0.50 is a floor, not a judgement.
notes: Scoring is near-degenerate. 8/07 replay: 29 SweepPrints on the day — 23 at exactly 3 levels (conf 0.50), 5 at 4 (0.67), 1 at 6 (1.00). So 79% of sweeps score IDENTICALLY at the floor, and 0.50 carries no information beyond 'it qualified'. Sizes: min 100 (the SWEEP_MIN_SIZE floor), median 123, max 926 — size is the discriminating axis and the confidence formula ignores it entirely (min(1.0, ticks/(2*SWEEP_MIN_TICKS)) is levels-only). Day count 29 is inside the ~10-40 rarity band st-wnc targeted, so the FLOOR is calibrated fine; it's the SCORE that needs a size term. title: Strader: live footprint — expanding an emitter message kills progressive rendering until reload
description:
REPORTED by Steve 2026-08-07 on /tmp/desk-live-footprint.html.

SYMPTOM: click one of the header row's down-arrows to expand an emitter message and the progressive build stops. Collection keeps running and the bar count keeps climbing, and pressing 'Bar >' still advances the display manually, but nothing renders on its own again until a full window reload.

HYPOTHESIS (traced, NOT reproduced — verify before fixing). In scripts/orderflow_drill_template.html:
  line 339   let liveFollow = true;   // auto-advance to the newest bar as it lands
  line 1346  if (liveFollow && wasAtTip) { while (idx < bars.length - 1) step(); }
  line 1395  function noteSeek() { liveFollow = idx >= bars.length - 1; ... }

Expanding an emitter message very likely seeks to the bar that emitted it, which calls noteSeek() while idx is behind the tip, so liveFollow flips false and the pollBars auto-advance at 1346 stops firing.

WHY 'Bar >' DOES NOT RECOVER IT — this is the part that makes it a trap rather than a nuisance: liveFollow is only restored by a seek that lands with idx >= bars.length-1, and the tip is MOVING. Step forward manually and new bars land while you are stepping, so idx never catches bars.length-1 and liveFollow stays false forever. Reload is the only escape, which matches the report.

FIX DIRECTIONS (pick after reproducing):
- Expanding an emission should not be a seek at all — reading what a bar said is not the same as navigating to it.
- If it must seek, restore follow with a tolerance (idx >= bars.length - 1 - N) or re-arm it when the user reaches the newest bar by any means.
- Surface the state: liveFollow=false should be visible in the bridge-dot readout ('paused at bar N of M') instead of silently looking identical to a stalled feed. Steve could not tell the difference between 'not following' and 'nothing arriving', which is the actual cost of this bug.

Page is generated by scripts/live_footprint_page.py from scripts/orderflow_drill_template.html; the .live mode gate hides drill-only controls, so check whether the emission disclosure is even meant to be interactive in live mode.
close_reason: Reproduced headlessly (tools/live_follow_check.mjs), fixed, verified. Root cause was the traced hypothesis: the tape marker's seekTo() landed idx behind a MOVING tip, noteSeek turned liveFollow off, and step() never re-armed it. Fix: reading a marked bar no longer seeks in LIVE (replay keeps it); the panel got its own anchor so an arriving bar cannot repoint it; the readout now says '⏸ holding at bar N of M — click to follow' and that click is the guaranteed way back. New check reproduces the old behaviour exactly and passes 16/16 on the fix. Commit 7441af8.

title: Strader: session rituals read claims, not observations — surface liveness probe
description:
Steve resubscribed GEXBot the afternoon of 2026-08-05. The session spent the rest of the day telling him we had no GEX while the collector was writing to data/corpus/2026-08-05/gexbot.jsonl in the next tmux window. Nothing was broken and nobody was careless: the belief came from an auto-memory file and a CurrentStatus line that were both true when written.

This is the SAME failure the tap-in skill already warns about for the beads export (co-vf9q): 'plausible, well-formed, wrong data, which is worse than returning nothing.' CurrentStatus.md is a claim about the world; the session had no step that observed it.

SHIPPED: scripts/surface_liveness.sh — dependency-free (ps/ls/date only, so it cannot itself be the thing that is down), read-only, safe mid-session. Probes ES capture, drill bridge, footprint feeder, GEX collector, MI gauge, and the day's corpus artifacts with sizes and mtimes. Wired into tap-in as step 4b, immediately after CurrentStatus, with the explicit rule that the observation wins where the two disagree.

The operator should never have to remember to circle the agent in.

FOUND ON FIRST RUN, which is the point:
- ES capture correctly DOWN — the supervisor's 15:05 stop worked, tape closed at 152M / MBP-1 3.2G.
- GEX collector running under a DIFFERENT pid than earlier in the session (1705645 vs 1669196), so it had been restarted without anyone noticing.
- Bridge and feeder still UP after 9h17m, tailing a file that stopped growing at 15:05 — the stale-stack condition from this morning, benign now but the same shape.

FOLLOW-ON worth its own bead: the live-footprint stack has no daily lifecycle. The feeder resolves its corpus day at startup and the bridge accumulates that day's bars in memory, so both are pinned to the day they were launched and must be restarted each morning. Nothing does that — capture is now supervised, its two consumers are not. Bring the stack up with scripts/live-footprint-up.sh at the start of each session day.

title: GexBot distiller V2 — dead zero_gamma path + width-only regime heuristic
description:

2. WIDTH-ONLY REGIME IS TREND-BLIND: 2026-06-09 was a ~190pt trend-down session; the distiller called 'pinning' on 180/291 RTH cycles (trending: 1) because the majors bracket stayed <50pt wide while SLIDING with price — opening bracket 7435-7480, price below it 281/281 later minutes. ## Acceptance Criteria
- on_flip sourced from a field that actually arrives; loud warning when missing
- Regime logic incorporates bracket drift and/or vol direction; replayed against the 06-09 capture it must NOT call a 190pt slide 'pinning' for the majority of RTH

The value is highest in exactly the quiet stretches the fly play lives in (the 10:00-13:00 consolidation and the approach to a V), and it would show a flush BUILDING mid-bar instead of only after 2000 contracts complete.

THE PIECES ALREADY EXIST:
1. live_footprint_feed.py already tees every trade into pending_trades, and take_bar_trades pops the closed bar's slice — so pending_trades IS the developing bar's trade list, already ordered and deduped.
2. build_bars(iter(pending), n=N, include_partial=True) yields EXACTLY ONE partial bar. Verified: 30 trades / 300 contracts against N=2000 gives 1 bar with correct o/h/l/c, delta and cells. Same code path as a closed bar, so a developing column cannot render differently from the closed one it becomes.
3. The per-trade hook exists: the main loop blocks inside build_bars between closes, but the _tee generator runs on every trade. A wall-clock check there (say 1s) is the natural emit point — single-threaded, no new concurrency.

TRANSPORT: the bridge gains a 'developing' field, REPLACED not appended, cleared when the next closed bar lands. Mirrors how 'final' was added for st-b0n9.

TEMPLATE: hold it in its own variable and render it as one extra ghost column AFTER the last real column. It must NEVER be pushed into the bars array — that sidesteps every bars.length / idx / seek / episode-scan interaction, which is exactly where the bugs would be. Style it as provisional (dashed border or reduced opacity) so a developing bar is never mistaken for a closed one, and show its running delta prominently, since a delta building mid-bar is the actual signal.

PARITY GUARDRAIL — THE PART THAT MATTERS. The developing bar is DISPLAY-ONLY. It must never enter the bars array, never drive StackDriver, and never reach the replay record. Running the recognizer on a partial bar would corrupt its engagement state, and running the engine twice over the same trades would double-emit. StackDriver's docstring already documents the one known live/replay divergence (the trailing partial bar at stream end); a display-only channel adds no new one. No emissions on the developing bar.

BOOT SAFETY: per ea77d7a, the developing field is absent most of the time and always absent at boot — every access guarded, and the page must render correctly with it null.

DEPLOY TIMING: needs a feeder restart, and the feeder re-reads the day file from the start, so it re-posts every bar — meaning the bridge must be restarted with it or the bars duplicate. Do it after the 15:05 stop, not mid-session. (Worth a separate look: the feeder having no resume point is a wart in its own right.)
