title: Strader: recognizer has no upside mirror — every setup is a downside form, and Mancini resistances enter as support
description:
Steve, watching the live footprint 2026-08-05 with ES trading UP through Mancini's resistance ladder, asked whether we differentiate 'breakdown' from 'breakout'. We do not, and the gap is two-layered. Both layers were live and firing at the moment he asked.

LAYER 1 — NO UPSIDE SETUP EXISTS. SetupRecognizer's whole vocabulary is downside: failed_breakdown, level_reclaim, range_trap, return_to_lvn. Each engages on a flush BELOW an anchor and a recovery back above. There is no failed_breakout / bull-trap mirror (price pushes ABOVE a level, fails to hold, returns beneath it). Every recognition emitted today carried bias=bullish; the recognizer structurally cannot produce a bearish read.

LAYER 2 — ANCHOR KIND IS DISCARDED (this is st-tme, already open). market/orderflow/anchors.py::parsed_mancini_levels returns prices only and day_anchors admits every Mancini level as kind='support'. Verified live: all 51 of today's Mancini anchors are 'support', including the 12 the parse recorded as RESISTANCE — 7783, 7790, 7803, 7815, 7826, 7835, 7846, 7855, 7867, 7875, 7882, 7894.

WHAT STEVE ACTUALLY SAW: 'failed_breakdown forming @ 7815.00 (support ∩ mancini)'. 7815 is a resistance in today's parse. Price had pushed above 7815 and fallen back beneath it — which at a resistance is a FAILED BREAKOUT, a bear signal — and the recognizer labelled it a bullish failed-breakdown forming, i.e. it would read the reclaim as a long. Same price action, opposite meaning, because the anchor kind is wrong AND no upside form exists to classify it as.

This is a systemic direction inversion in the tooling — the mirror image of the operator error mode in knowledge/direction-inversion-watch.md, and it deserves the same treatment: verify the anchor first.

WHY IT BITES HARDEST TODAY: ES is parabolic at all-time highs, so the entire level ladder price is interacting with is overhead resistance. The anchor set is inverted in kind for precisely the levels in play.

NAMING DECISION TO SETTLE (Steve's actual question): when the mirror lands, does the emitted setup stay 'failed_breakdown' or become 'failed_breakout'? st-tme's acceptance criteria says resistance anchors 'engage upward-mirrored recognition' but does not say whether the NAME changes. It must — 'failed_breakdown' on a resistance engagement is unreadable, and per knowledge/establish-before-abbreviate.md a Steve-facing term has to say what it means. Mancini's own vocabulary: 'Failed Breakdown' is the long; he calls the level-loss short a 'breakdown trade'. Proposed: failed_breakout for the upside mirror, with the stage names (flush/stall/flip/confirm) reading in the mirrored direction.

INTERIM MITIGATION WORTH CONSIDERING, cheap and low-risk: kind-filter the live/drill anchor set to supports only, which is what the acuity path ALREADY does (acuity_run2.py letter_levels_for) and what anchors.py's own same-anchor-rule docstring claims. That removes the wrong signal without inventing the mirror, whose introduction st-tme requires a full acuity re-sweep for. Silence beats an inverted direction label on a surface Steve trades from. NOT applied unilaterally — it changes live signal output.

Depends on / overlaps st-tme (Anchor Kind Fidelity).

title: Strader: session-scale cumulative delta has no directional edge — baseline measured
description:
Run-down of the 2026-08-04 claim that the day's 129-point rally was 'bought by nobody' on negative cumulative delta. Written up in docs/measurement/cumulative-delta-session-baseline.md.

FIRST, THE TOOLING IS CLEAN. Two things were suspected and both cleared:
- Aggressor sign inversion: tested against our own MBP-1 top-of-book, matching each trade to the last quote strictly before it. 'A' printed at/below the bid 100.0% (16,362 trades, 14:00-14:10 UTC) and 'B' at/above the ask 100.0%; reproduced on a second window (7,597 trades, 19:30-19:40). Zero ambiguous prints. trade.py's docstring and bars.py agree with the venue. Delta is NOT inverted.
- Live/replay divergence: both live bridge readings reproduce EXACTLY from the corpus — as of 13:45:22 (525 bars, close 7769.75 at 13:44:35, fly slice +1.50, delta -1,453) and as of 14:46:00 (593 bars, close 7783.75 at 14:45:58, fly slice +15.50, delta -7,856). The apparent discrepancy was my own reconciliation error: comparing a 13:00-14:46 live window against a 13:00-13:45 corpus window.

THE FINDING. Over 21 full corpus days: ES carries a persistent POSITIVE aggressor tilt — 17 of 21 days positive, median +1.11% of session volume. That baseline exists nowhere in the codebase or on the charts, which is why a -0.50% day got narrated as dramatic.

corr(session delta%, day price change) = -0.22, n=21. Slightly inverse, effectively noise. 07-27 ran +1.53% delta and closed -58.50; 07-29 +0.82% and -106.00; 08-03 +0.17% and +82.25; 08-04 -0.50% and +129.00. Session-scale delta carries NO directional edge in our own data.

2026-08-04 specifically: -0.50%, 2nd lowest of 21 — unusual as a LEVEL, not a direction. Buy-aggressor share was still 49.75%, the most extreme single hour was +7.51% (a BUYING hour, near the top of the sample), and 14:46->close ran +4,365.

SCOPE LIMIT, deliberately: this says nothing about delta at BAR and LEVEL scale, which is where SetupRecognizer actually uses it (flush/stall/flip/confirm) and where absorption reads live. Different time scale, different claim. Do not generalise into 'delta is useless'.

FOLLOW-UP: 21 days is one regime, all of it inside a strong uptrend. Re-run as the corpus grows. Worth deciding whether the +1.11% baseline should be surfaced on the live footprint so a delta reading is glanceable against its norm rather than against zero.

title: Strader: nightly GLBX backfill — fill the hours live capture does not cover
description:
Second half of the st-btu ruling (2026-08-05): live capture covers 02:50-15:05 CT, everything else is backfilled. The supervisor half shipped in 6238bb1; this is the backfill half.

WHY IT IS FREE: GLBX historical measures $0.0000 under the current Databento Futures plan. Measured via --estimate-only (metadata.get_cost, pulls nothing): ES trades and mbp-1 for the 08-05 02:50-06:45 gap, and mbp-1 for a full settled day (07-31 02:50-15:05), all $0.0000 — against an OPRA control of $6.0663 for a 2h window, which proves the estimator returns non-zero when it should. Re-estimate before each run anyway; a plan change would silently turn this into spend.

SCOPE: for a completed day D, pull GLBX ES trades + mbp-1 for the hours outside 02:50-15:05 and append into data/corpus/D/. Pullers already exist: scripts/corpus_pull_databento_es.py and corpus_pull_databento_es_mbp1.py, both taking --start-ct/--end-ct and --estimate-only.

TWO CONSTRAINTS THAT DECIDE THE DESIGN:

1. APPEND IS SAFE FOR REPLAY, NOT FOR LIVE. read_corpus_day sorts by (ts, sequence) and dedups on read (market/orderflow/replay.py), so historical rows appended out of order behind live rows are re-sorted and harmless to every replay/measurement consumer. But live_footprint_feed.py TAILS the same file through a 2s reorder buffer — historical rows arriving mid-session are wildly out of order, and build_bars raises on out-of-order. So the backfill must NEVER run while a feeder is tailing that day. Run it after the 15:05 stop, or gate it on the supervisor reporting no live capture for the target day.

2. sequence IS NULL on this feed (verified in the 08-04 rows), so the sort degrades to timestamp-only and is stable. Dedup is on dedup_key; a re-run must be idempotent, and the live/historical overlap at the window edges is exactly where duplicates will land.

ALSO WORTH DECIDING: whether to backfill the 15:05->23:59 evening Globex into day D's dir and 00:00->02:50 into day D+1's, which is what the day-dir convention implies, or to treat the Globex session as its own unit. The corpus convention is calendar-day dirs, so per-day windows is the lower-friction choice.

FIRST RUN: 2026-08-05 02:50-06:45 CT is the gap left by this morning's dead capture — a real, already-identified target to validate against, and free.

title: Strader: CLAUDE.md frames flies as range-centered — the reason the directional correction keeps failing
description:
Steve has corrected the fly framing at least three times (claude-monitor record: 2026-06-09T17:16, 2026-06-24T21:39, 2026-06-24T22:02, plus 2026-05-06T15:37) and it recurred again 2026-08-05.

ROOT CAUSE, and why memory did not stop it: CLAUDE.md is loaded every session and is declared authoritative ('OVERRIDE any default behavior... follow exactly as written'). It describes strike selection as 'centering butterflies relative to the consolidation range' (line 199) and 'A butterfly centered in the consolidation range' (line 112). The auto-memory feedback_directional_gex_flies.md ALREADY diagnosed this in July — 'CLAUDE.md describes flies in textbook price-neutral terms; Steve's actual method is directional' — but nobody fixed the source. Instructions outrank memory by construction, so every session re-inherits the wrong frame and the correction has to be re-issued by hand.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG: the mechanics in The Play are RIGHT — buy after the sharp drop when the fly is cheap, it reprices on the rally back. That is buying movement. What misleads is the centering language, which reads as though range-boundedness is the PRECONDITION. It is not. The precondition is a departure and a return (V-dump-and-return), or distance to a GEX magnet with room to travel. Steve: 'I'm not looking to center and hold. I'm buying late to buy the movement.' And verbatim: 'so you say: Fly wants: isn't the fly i want.'

THE 2026-08-05 RECURRENCE reproduced that exact construction — 'the consolidation range a fly wants to center on' — and inverted the conclusion, treating a market extended far from support as hostile to flies when distance-from-target is what makes the fly cheap and gives it room.

FIX: make CLAUDE.md state the frame explicitly (directional, delta not theta, movement not range-occupancy) so the always-loaded instruction stops contradicting the knowledge bundle. Mirror the banned framing into knowledge/directional-gex-butterflies.md.
close_reason: Fixed the source, not just the symptom. CLAUDE.md now states the fly as directional movement-buying: body at the DESTINATION (V-return level or GEX magnet), consolidation range as the landmark that identifies it rather than a requirement, delta not theta, precondition = departure-and-return not range occupancy, both entry engines named, 3/5-lot with a runner. Banned-framing block added there and mirrored into knowledge/directional-gex-butterflies.md with Steve's three corrections verbatim from the claude-monitor record; knowledge/log.md entry appended. Auto-memory feedback_directional_gex_flies.md updated with the same ban plus a pointer to check the CLAUDE.md edit survived if the framing ever reappears. Commit 9d393af.

THE STALE-STACK TRAP IS ITS OWN DEFECT: a live page whose feeder tails a finished prior-day file renders a quiet tape, not an error. That is st-6qx4's named gap ('bridge and feeder are unsupervised so a dead feeder freezes the live page looking like a quiet tape') — now observed, not hypothetical.

RESOLUTION TODAY: started capture in pane 1 with yesterday's exact invocation (--streams es,es-mbp1 --until-ct 15:05 --now) so no capture-window ruling was implied; restarted bridge then feeder so today's bars do not append onto yesterday's 690 in bridge memory.

title: Strader: emissions panel review follow-ups — conf 0.00, beats/stages, panel clips readouts
description:
Three items Steve raised reviewing the live emissions panel in-browser 2026-08-04.

1. CONF 0.00 — an invalidated SetupRecognition carries confidence 0.0 (recognizer.py line 300), so the panel's Conf column renders a meaningless '0.00'. For an invalidated setup confidence is not-applicable, not zero. Render an em dash. Keep it precise to invalidated recognitions rather than blanket-hiding any 0.00, which would mask a genuine zero elsewhere.

2. BEATS -> STAGES — the recognizer's own reason strings still say 'beats so far: flush+flip' and 'no reclaim (beats: ...)'. That text renders in the panel's 'why the stack said it' column, so it is Steve-facing, and 'beats' is the banned term (musical collision; the four-part sequence is STAGES). The UI labels already say stages; the backend string did not get the memo.

   CONSEQUENCE: reason is a serialized Signal field, so it is IN the parity snapshot (expected_signals_20260702.json carries 'beats so far: flush' and 'beats so far: flush+flip'). Changing it requires a deliberate regeneration via scripts/regen_parity_snapshot.py --reason, one commit with the CHANGES.md entry, per the parity.py docstring.

   OUT OF SCOPE HERE: the dataclass FIELD is also named 'beats', as are the recognizer internals and the template's inst.beats / renderBeatRail. Renaming the field touches the replay records, the anatomy payload and the template together — that belongs to st-g9y (PA vocabulary consistency review), not to a text fix.

3. PANEL CLIPS THE READOUTS — #empanel is absolutely positioned inside .controls, so a tall panel's bottom edge lands mid-way through the readouts row and cuts the text. Worst of both: the Bar/Time/Last/Delta context is neither visible nor cleanly covered. The panel header already restates bar number and clock, so covering the block cleanly is no loss.
close_reason: All three shipped in 7a1c5c6. (1) Invalidated setups render an em dash instead of a meaningless 0.00, kept narrow to that case. (2) Recognizer reason strings say 'stages' not 'beats'; parity snapshot regenerated deliberately with CHANGES.md entry — diff verified as 4 lines, one word each, all in 'reason', no threshold/logic/ordering change. Field name still 'beats' — left to st-g9y as noted. (3) Panel's containing block is now #ctlblock (controls+readouts+emrow) with min-height:100%, so it covers whole rows instead of cutting the readouts mid-line. tools/drill_page_check.mjs gained assertions for all three; 19/19 clean on 2026-07-31, live page boots clean empty, 830 pass.

title: Strader: live footprint header reads '0 contracts' all session
description:

description:
st-b0n9 made market.orderflow.anchors.mancini_levels_for fall back to the day's own parse artifact (runbook/mancini/parsed/<day>.json) when the hand-labeled corpus does not cover the day.

WHY IT WAS NEEDED: the labeled corpus (docs/measurement/mancini-setup-labels-2026-07-06.json, the st-3vu validated source) stops at the study days. Every recent session resolved to ZERO Mancini anchors, so a live recognizer watched nothing but range edges. On 2026-08-04 the fallback loads 78 levels where the old rule loaded 0, and the live surface went from ~0 to 139 emissions across 322 bars.

SAFE BY PRECEDENCE: labeled days are untouched — the labeled corpus still wins wherever it covers the day, so no validated result moved.

WHAT NEEDS A DECISION: unlabeled days now produce DIFFERENT anchors than they did before, which means (a) the drill surface and (b) session_record.py's measured record both change for recent days. Records are append-only so nothing was rewritten, but a new run over a recent day will not match an older run of that same day, and the difference is the anchor set rather than a code change to the engine. Anyone comparing runs across that boundary needs to know.

ALSO: parsed_mancini_levels reads PRICES ONLY. The parse carries a 'kind' per level and admits every one as 'support', matching day_anchors' existing rule. Carrying resistance through as a downward-mirrored engagement is st-tme's job — doing it in the loader would change what the recognizer fires on without the measurement st-tme is holding for.

PROPOSAL: decide whether recent days should be re-recorded under the new anchor rule, and whether the fallback should be labeled in RunMeta so a reader can tell which anchor source a run used.

title: Strader: page boot check into CI — declare a JS runtime for tools/page_boot_check.mjs
description:
tools/page_boot_check.mjs (added under st-b0n9) boots a desk page in a headless DOM and fails on the first uncaught error. It reproduces and CATCHES the exact defect that blanked the live footprint for a session (ea77d7a): removing the price!=null guard in the level-chip loop makes it exit 1 with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading toFixed)'.

It is NOT wired into any gate, because it needs node + jsdom and this repo declares no JS runtime. Constraints found: jsdom does NOT run under bun (its vm rejects a Proxy in the global prototype chain), and jsdom >= 25 needs a newer node than the nvm default here. Working combination is node 20 + jsdom@24, installed out-of-tree:

  cd <scratch> && bun add jsdom@24
  NODE_PATH=<scratch>/node_modules node tools/page_boot_check.mjs /tmp/desk-live-footprint.html

DECISION NEEDED (COO owns structural authority here, and st-lh3 'default to bun as JS/TS runtime across zgent repos' is the open convention proposal this collides with): bun cannot host jsdom, so either the JS-runtime convention admits node for DOM testing, or the boot check moves to a different engine (happy-dom, or a real headless Chrome).

Until it is wired, the check only runs when someone remembers. The failure mode it guards is silent and expensive: the page renders its chrome and sits empty, which reads as a network fault and is not one.

title: Strader: Live emissions panel — what the stack emitted at a given bar, on rollover
description:
Steve 2026-08-04, after first successfully watching the live footprint paint: he wants the bars to carry a way to replay WHAT WAS EMITTED at a given point in time. Proposed UI: a header row plus a rollover control that opens a panel sitting over the existing control strip (Level / Arm level / Rows / Cells / Table view / Anatomy / ?).

SCOPE WARNING — this is NOT a UI tweak. scripts/live_footprint_feed.py imports only bars, fill, replay and config; it does NOT run OrderflowEngine, find_stacks or SetupRecognizer. The live path currently produces bars and nothing else, so there are no emissions to display. The work is putting the full stack into the live path, then carrying its output to the page.

REUSE, DO NOT REIMPLEMENT. market/orderflow/parity.py already defines THE canonical pipeline as full_stack_events(...) — reader-ordered trades, volume bars, engine signals, per-bar imbalances, recognizer events, profile levels, in a documented stable order — and the st-bw9 harness snapshots it field-by-field in CI. market/orderflow/session_record.py runs that same production stack over a corpus day and appends every emission to data/measurement/replay/. The live feeder must drive full_stack_events, not a parallel path, or the live surface and the replay record can disagree and every drilled rep stops transferring.

DESIGN QUESTION to settle first: attach emissions to their bar in the existing /bars payload, or carry them on a separate bridge channel keyed by bar index? Bars are already pushed on close and the page holds them in an array, so attaching is simpler and keeps one ordering; a separate channel is better if emissions can arrive after their bar (engine flush(), profile levels emitted at end of stream). Probably attach per-bar, plus a small end-of-stream channel for flush emissions.

NOTE for whoever builds it: the drill template's boot path is fragile with sparse data — three live-only crashes were fixed in ea77d7a, all from fields a replay always populates. Any new panel must tolerate a bar with zero emissions, which will be the common case.

WHY IT WAITED: raised mid-session with context nearly exhausted, and nothing is lost by deferring — scripts/replay_day.py gives the full emission record for today after the close, and its docstring notes the batch pass is byte-identical to a paced live run over the same tape.
close_reason:
Live emissions panel shipped, commit 383c4a1. Backend + UI both done; running live on today's tape at handoff (322 bars, 112 carrying 139 emissions, most recent a failed_breakdown confirmed @ 7727.00 support-and-mancini at 10:38:48).

DESIGN QUESTION SETTLED (the bead asked): emissions ride ON the bar as 'ev', not a separate channel. Bars are already pushed on close and held in an indexed array, so attaching keeps one ordering and one arrival — a bar and what it emitted can never be out of step or half-delivered. End-of-stream emissions (engine flush, profile levels) belong to no bar and DO take a separate 'final' channel, held like meta so a page opened after the close still receives them.

REUSE HELD. parity.full_stack_events was not copied — it was split. StackDriver is the canonical drive loop as an incremental object, and full_stack_events is now a thin caller that only slices trades to bars. The committed parity snapshot came out byte-identical, and a new test asserts bar-by-bar drive equals full_stack_events over the same tape.

THREE THINGS THE LIVE PATH NEEDED THAT DID NOT EXIST:
1. ProfileAccumulator (profile.py) — build_profile now delegates to it. Live has one trade at a time and no end; holding every trade to rebuild at the close costs hundreds of MB over an ES day.
2. LiveAnchors (anchors.py) — day_anchors wants the session high/low, which a replay knows on bar 0 and live cannot. Mancini levels fixed, range edges develop and converge on the replay set by the close. An edge FREEZES while engaged: it breaks exactly when a new extreme prints, so moving it mid-read means no range_trap could ever complete. Anchor is frozen, so the move is a swap via the new SetupRecognizer.retarget, which owns the idle guard and carries confluence + fire history across.
3. Mancini parse fallback — the labeled corpus stops at the study days, so every recent session had ZERO anchors and the recognizer watched only range edges. 2026-08-04 went 0 -> 78 anchors. Labeled days untouched. Filed st-ispq for the measured-record consequence.

KNOWN DIVERGENCE, DOCUMENTED IN CODE: full_stack_events builds with include_partial=True, so a day's trailing under-N bar is a real bar carrying its own stacks and recognitions. The live feeder renders closed bars only, so those trades reach finish() as trailing trades with bar_i=None and no stacks/recognitions. Only the final partial bar of a session differs; every closed bar agrees exactly. Deliberately NOT changed — switching the live feeder to include_partial would alter v1 render behaviour on a running surface mid-session.

BOOT SAFETY. Every field access in the panel is guarded, because ea77d7a traced three live-only boot crashes to fields a replay always populates, and emissions are exactly that shape (sparse, optional, absent for most of a session). Added tools/page_boot_check.mjs, which boots a page in a headless DOM and fails on the first uncaught error — and VERIFIED it catches the original defect (drop the price!=null guard in the chip loop, it exits 1 on 'undefined reading toFixed'). Not gated yet; needs a declared JS runtime, filed as st-0ic4.

STACK RESTARTED to pick the code up: bridge (pane 0) and feeder (pane 2) only, during the 10:00-13:00 no-trade window. CAPTURE (pane 1, pid 496170) was never touched — that is the irreplaceable half.

NOT DONE: Steve has not eyeballed the panel in a real browser yet. jsdom proves it boots, renders chips, opens on rollover, pins on click, and survives an empty bar and a walk to the tip with zero errors — but that is not the same as him looking at it.

title: Strader: Preclude Schwab streaming structurally; cross-source reconciliation for Schwab REST
description: Steve 2026-08-03, re: peer misgivings about Schwab streaming feeds. FINDING — we do not use Schwab streaming at all. market/corpus/schwab_stream.py is misnamed: it is pull_cycle(), REST polling, not a stream. The only schwab.streaming.StreamClient consumer in the repo is scripts/stream_to_excel.py, and that script is ALREADY DEAD — line 91 calls client.get_account_numbers(), which the hobbled-readonly fork structurally removed, so it raises AttributeError before ever opening a socket. Consequences: (1) whatever Schwab's streaming-vs-TOS concurrency rule is, we do not trigger it today; (2) precluding Schwab streaming costs us nothing currently in use. PROPOSED: delete scripts/stream_to_excel.py and remove schwab/streaming.py from the fork with a DEFENSE NOTE entry, making 'no Schwab streaming' structural rather than policy — the same doctrine already applied to orders and accounts. The one real cost to name in the note: streaming is the only path to sub-minute Schwab data (e.g. tick-resolution $TICK rather than minute candles), so this forecloses that option until deliberately reversed. ALSO: rename schwab_stream.py -> schwab_poll.py; the current name is what made this question ambiguous. SEPARATE HALF — guard the REST polling we DO depend on. Schwab uniquely supplies NYSE internals ($TICK/$TRIN/$ADD/$VOLD/$VIX minute candles) and 0DTE chain/ATM snapshots; the internals are SINGLE-SOURCED with no cross-check, which is the real exposure. Databento now covers ES and OPRA independently, so spot_es and the option tape CAN be reconciled against it. Build a divergence check over the overlap.

title: Bar-level dip-entry chase sim (join-the-turn) with cooldown
description:
Follow-on from Grade The Flush (st-gzwb). The one execution shape under which Steve's tight-cut + liberal re-entry contention could still work is entry ON the backtest (join the counter-move's turn back toward trend) rather than on the breakout — it inverts the refill geometry so each failed cycle risks ~turn+stop instead of paying the wiggle amplitude. The tick-level probe in scripts/measurement/morning_flush_study.py churned (0.75-pt turn is inside ES bid-ask bounce; 300+ attempts/day artifact even with cooldown).

## What to build
Re-implement the dip_entry mode of simulate() on 5s or 15s bar closes instead of raw ticks, with (a) DIP_TURN swept 1.5/2/3 pts, (b) post-stop cooldown = fresh counter-extreme beyond the stop, (c) campaign staleness guard so it stops trading after the move is structurally over (no re-arm once price is >2x R_END off the campaign extreme), (d) attempt caps 2 and 5. title: Strader: listlevels regex drops levels when Mancini's (major) paren is unclosed
description: Found during the 2026-08-03 in-session parse (st-26q5). The deterministic scrape returned 31 supports where the letter's 'Supports are:' sentence lists 33. The two dropped are 7374 and 7353 — both annotated (major), and both are entries where Mancini left the paren unclosed: '7374 (major, 7364' and '7353 (major, 7341'. listlevels.extract_list_levels presumably requires a closed ')' to terminate the annotation, so the malformed entry and its price are skipped. Severity: these are not random drops — an unclosed paren only ever happens on a (major) annotation, so the failure mode selectively eats MAJOR levels, which are the ones that matter most. Resistances were unaffected (30/30) because that sentence had no typos. Fix: tolerate an unterminated annotation — treat ',' or the next digit run as a terminator as well as ')'. Add a regression fixture built from the 08-03 supports sentence verbatim, typos included. Until fixed, any hybrid-mode (levels-only) publication can silently omit major levels.

title: Speech phrasebook: render emitted Signals as sentences meant to be heard, not read
description:
Origin: COO session 2026-08-02, Steve's direction. Step 1 of 4 on the voice-output path; audio substrate already proven under COO co-fsg5p.

The emitter puts out typed Signals, each carrying a human-readable 'reason'. That reason is written to be READ. Speech needs a separate rendering, for three reasons:

1. reason uses measurement-harness vocabulary (anchor, fire, stage names). st-v95 exists because that vocabulary reached Steve undefined. Spoken output must use the plain-words glossary (docs/training/plain-words-glossary.md), which is the authority.
2. Prices must be spoken the way a trader says them. '7438.25' read aloud as 'seven thousand four hundred thirty eight point two five' is both wrong and too slow to be useful mid-tape.
3. LIVE vs HINDSIGHT is a safety property, not a style choice. The glossary marks percentiles, cells, legs and archetypes as HINDSIGHT — computable only after the day completes. Speaking a HINDSIGHT quantity in real time asserts something unknowable. The phrasebook must refuse to.

Scope is deliberately narrow: a pure function, Signal -> spoken string or None. No audio, no queue, no policy about what is worth saying. Testable by printing.

Explicit non-goals (later steps, separate beads): speech policy / what earns an utterance; the staleness queue that drops utterances gone stale before their turn; the reader process and barge-in; any live wiring. First real use is replay drills, not live trading — nothing consumes signals in a live loop today.

## Acceptance Criteria

[ ] spoken_price renders ES quarter-tick prices trader-style: 7438.0 -> 'seventy-four thirty-eight', 7438.25 -> '... and a quarter', 7400.0 -> 'seventy-four hundred', 7405.0 -> 'seventy-four oh five'
[ ] Number words are generated in-process, not delegated to the TTS engine, so output does not vary by engine
[ ] Every orderflow Signal subclass has phrasing: SweepPrint, DeltaDivergence, ImbalanceStack, AbsorptionRead, SetupRecognition
[ ] SetupRecognition speaks the fire count when above 1 — st-m3f makes the fourth fire a materially different call from the first, and a voice that hides it is misleading
[ ] Beat tokens (flush/stall/flip/confirm) render as plain words, never as the frozen tokens
[ ] An unrecognised Signal subclass returns None and logs; it never guesses
[ ] No HINDSIGHT quantity can be emitted
[ ] Unit tests cover each subclass plus the price edge cases

title: Overnight interaction brief — how overnight PA treated the prior letter's levels, appended to the parsed plan
description:
Steve directive 2026-07-28: Mancini writes his letter at or near end-of-day on the day BEFORE the session the plan targets. By RTH open, overnight price action has always already interacted with the levels he referenced — some tested, some broken, some reclaimed. The parsed plan needs a supplemental section that spells this out, so the morning brief reads as "here is the plan, and here is what has already happened to it."

## Method

- Data: Schwab minute bars via the read-only client (lib/schwab-py get_price_history_every_minute / every_five_minutes; token at tokens/schwab_token.json, 7-day lifecycle st-096 is the operational risk). Window: from the letter's generation time (~16:00 ET prior day) to now.
- Logic: new module runbook/mancini/overnight.py. For each level in the ParseResult, compute against the overnight bars: untouched / tested-and-held (bars touched within tolerance, closes stayed on the correct side) / broken (close beyond by > tolerance) / reclaimed (close back after a break), plus current distance from last price. Same close-based definitions the chart renderer uses, so the written brief and the chart never disagree.
- Output: an "## Overnight interaction" section appended to the desk plan doc (myDesk/reports/mancini/mancini-es-<date>.md -> stable title), listing only levels that were touched or better, most significant first (reclaimed > broken > tested), each with one plain-language line. Untouched levels are summarized in a single count line.
- Runs as part of the on-request morning parse (the parse contract in conventions/mancini-parse-is-prompt-driven.md gains a step 5b); degrades gracefully to "overnight data unavailable" if the Schwab token is dead — never blocks the parse.

## Acceptance Criteria

- runbook/mancini/overnight.py with unit tests (synthetic bars covering each state transition and the tolerance boundary).
- The desk plan doc for a real parse day carries the section; stable title updated as part of the existing publish step.
- Parse contract convention updated (COO repo) once live.
- Token-dead path verified: parse completes, section says data unavailable.

title: X-ray harness: deterministic watcher 90%, interactive agent switched on at pivotal moments
description: Steve role ruling 2026-07-27: he is sole risk/sizing authority but NOT the arbiter of PA correctness — authoritative confirmation is hindsight measurement (replay record + acuity sweep). Agent attention must not cover the whole session; duty-cycle it. Design: Phase B live stack runs all session unattended (st-d5f); thin trigger layer watches its own emissions — episode flush (primary tripwire), absorption/divergence clusters at a level, bar-pace acceleration, proximity to plan/GEX levels — and wakes an interactive session with a warm packet (recent bars payload, episode stage state, developing day type, plan levels) via the drill-bridge machinery (st-ago, port 7788). Agent evaluates the moment, speaks to desk, logs append-only, stands down. Live reads are graded by the same hindsight harness as the recognizer (acuity sweep) — agent accuracy becomes a measured stream. Duty-cycle evidence: 2026-07-22 had 5 episodes ≈ 25 min of pivotal time in 6.5h. v1 for 8/1: live recognizer 13:00-15:00 + [ALERT] rows to desk + standing coach session attending on alert; auto-wake orchestration is v2. title: FootPrint replay drills: re-run the week of DB RTH history as live sessions
description:
## Goal

With yesterday's session imported, we hold a full week of DataBento historical
RTH data. Build a replay capability that re-runs each day through the
classifier and recognizer code EXACTLY as if it were a live session — same
pacing, same FootPrint surface Steve watches live — recording all classifier
and recognizer output per day so it can be reviewed with 20/20 hindsight.

Steve will be in the chair for every replay: this is a drilling session for
him as much as a validation run for the recognizer. The session setup must be
indistinguishable from live watching.

## Why

- Review/audit of the recognizer code is warranted (Steve, 2026-07-25) — this
  produces the ground-truth record to audit against.
- Aligns with the standing harness-first directive (2026-07-16): coded harness
  over assisted in-session calculation.

## Scope of the NEXT step (not this bead's close condition)

A written plan (writing-plans flow) covering: replay clock/pacing model,
day-session setup and teardown, classifier+recognizer output capture format
and storage, how hindsight annotations attach, and the drill workflow from
Steve's seat. Plan first; implementation beads follow from the plan.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the imported RTH days can be launched as a replay session that is
  set up exactly like a live session from Steve's seat (FootPrint surface).
- Classifier and recognizer outputs are recorded per replayed day, reviewable
  after the fact.
- The drill workflow is documented (how Steve starts a day, watches, reviews).

## Constraints

- Replay must not contaminate live data paths or live session state.
- Recorded outputs are append-only per day (measured record, no rewrites).

title: Strader: MI composite gauge — internals-driven entry/exit scale (design + forward capture + drill integration)
description: Steve direction 2026-07-22: combine credible market-internals components into a single signed score that supports/blocks a given action, with exits as the primary use case (sell-into-climax discipline as the secondary indicator under Mancini level-to-level; sizing/runners remain the primary frame). Design constraints from Steve's profile: single number output BUT the dominant component must be named on the display (he learns patterns via drills, not formulas); condition-dependent weights allowed if kept to a small set of nameable market conditions, not continuous math. Components per credibility triage (2026-07-22 discussion): TICK percentile-of-recent-distribution (climax meter, core), cumulative TICK (day spine), ADD/VOLD (day-type context; ADD returned 0.0 via quote reader — investigate), our own CVD divergence from the orderflow engine as the non-classic fourth leg; TRIN excluded or trace weight. Phases: (A) data — probe Schwab price-history for $TICK/$ADD backfill; fix ADD zero; wire forward capture (REST polling, no streamer conflict) at stage boundaries + dense during action windows — internals are NOT backfillable if history probe fails, so forward capture starts before design settles (MBP-1 lesson). (B) score v1 hand-seeded weights, 3-4 named regimes (open drive / mid chop / power hour; internals-confirming vs diverging), tmux pane render + drill deck overlay. (C) calibrate on collected sessions, percentile thresholds. (D) rider study: .3-delta vs .6-delta singles comparison on the same measurement harness (Steve wants data before pushing back on the .6 default).
notes:
Phase A probe DONE 2026-07-22 (history.py reader written + run). FINDINGS: Schwab get_price_history serves minute candles for all four internals. $TICK: live intraday (~1 min lag) + backfill to a rolling ~47-day wall (2026-06-05 as of today, ~33 sessions) — calibration corpus exists NOW and drill-deck days within the window can carry a TICK overlay. $TRIN: same depth, live. $ADD + $VOLD: history fine through 2026-07-21 close but TODAY's session absent from both history and quotes (quote returns 0.0) — breadth feed lags or is T+0-dead; investigate before weighting ADD/VOLD in any live score (TICK+TRIN are the live-capable legs today). Volume field is always 0 on internals candles (expected — they have no volume). IMPLICATION for capture design: backfill exists but the window ROLLS — a weekly 45-day snapshot into the corpus preserves history permanently; dense live polling only needed for the current session's real-time gauge, and $TICK minute history may even substitute for live polling at 1-min granularity. New reader: broker_schwab/readers/history.py (read-only; needs allowlist entry to be auto-allowed like quote/chain).
2026-07-22 backfill + seed DONE: corpus_pull_internals.py written + run (31 sessions, 4 symbols, per-day internals.jsonl, weekly re-run makes the rolling window permanent); internals_calibrate.py computed the TICK percentile table; seeds persisted in market/signals/internals_config.py (bucket-conditioned CLIMAX=p95 / EXTREME=p99), findings in docs/measurement/internals-tick-seed-2026-07-22.md. Headline: folklore ±1000 is a ~1-in-10-sessions event (session-extreme marker, not per-minute signal); real climax line ≈ ±450-600 by bucket/side; open-drive positively skewed; afternoon negative tail deepest (p99 -892) = butterfly window. Remaining phase A: ADD/VOLD live-feed dead-today investigation; weekly snapshot scheduling. Phase B (score engine + tmux render + drill overlay) next.

DATA BUG FOUND+FIXED: Schwab same-day $TICK minutes are clamped (all lows/closes floored at 0 — same family as the ADD/VOLD dead-today issue) AND the just-settled day comes back DUPLICATED in one response (healed segment first, stale clamped segment second) — first-wins dedup in pull + reader, implausibility guard (full session with zero negative TICK minutes warns loudly), T+1 re-pull heals; --force refresh applied. CONSEQUENCE for live mode: same-day clamp means live gauge negative readings are UNRELIABLE from the minute-history endpoint intraday — live path needs the quote endpoint ($TICK last prints correctly, verified −46 on 7/22) polled directly instead; NOT yet fixed in scripts/mi_gauge.py --live. Live caveats stated at startup: sampled wicks understate extremes; mid-session launch = since-launch cum spine (start pane pre-open). title: Drill footer duration fill uses trailing-max normalization, inverting the pace read
description:
## Problem

`scripts/orderflow_drill_template.html` line ~397 sizes each footer's duration fill as `b.dur / trailingMaxDur(i)`, where `trailingMaxDur` maxes over the backward-only window `bars[i-KEEP_COLS+1 .. i]`. Any bar that is the running max of that window divides by itself and renders at 100% height.

Bar 0's window contains only itself, so bar 0 is always full height regardless of duration. On 2026-07-02 the first six bars run 2.0, 4.7, 10.1, 12.5, 14.0, 14.5s — monotonically increasing, so all six render full height. A 2.0s bar (fastest tape of the session; p10 is 13.7s) draws as maximally slow, inverting the legend 'tall fill = slow bar, short fill = urgent tape'.

Session-wide: 37 of 667 bars (5.5%) render full height on 7/2.

Secondary defect: the scale is relative and rebases every column, so equal heights mean different durations at different points in the day. That defeats absolute pace calibration, which is the pace strip's purpose.

Regression introduced by st-qen (footer absorbed the pace strip and inherited the standalone strip's relative normalization).

## Fix

Replace the trailing-window normalization with a fixed absolute ceiling constant across all days, sqrt-compressed for the skewed duration distribution (7/2: min 0.1, p25 20.5, median 30.8, p90 66.1, max 109.6s).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Footer fill height depends only on the bar's own duration and a module-level constant — no window lookup, no neighbor dependency.
- Bar 0 of 2026-07-02 (2.0s) renders a visible sliver, not full height.
- Median-duration bar renders near half height.
- Bars at/above the ceiling clamp to full height.
- Help overlay states the absolute anchor so full height is learnable.
- Drill regenerated for 2026-07-02 and visually verified.

title: Structural Leg Profiler study — measured evaluation against tick corpus
description:
# Structural Leg Profiler — Measured Evaluation Study Spec

Authored by COO (design-of-record) 2026-07-16 under **Leg Profiler Spec** (co-coui), at Steve's direction. Implementation is Strader's (Operating Officer for the trading system). Filed to Strader's tracker as a bead carrying this spec verbatim.

## Background

LuxAlgo's "Structural Leg Profiler" (https://www.luxalgo.com/library/indicator/structural-leg-profiler/) combines ATR-thresholded swing detection with per-leg volume profiles, per-leg POC, naked-POC forward projection, delta coloring, and volume-anomaly flags. It is closed-source and AI-generated (LuxAlgo Quant marketing demo — see transcript at Strader repo root `LuxAlgo_VolumeProfile.txt`), so nobody has validated it against data. Its behavior is fully specified by the page + transcript; we reimplement it deterministically and score its claims against Strader's tick corpus.

## What is being built

1. **Leg segmenter** — ATR-thresholded swing detection (ZigZag variant). Params: ATR period, swing multiplier. A leg CONFIRMS only when price reverses from its extreme by ≥ ATR × multiplier. No repaint: everything downstream scores from confirmation time, never retroactively.
2. **Per-leg volume profile** — histogram of trade volume across the leg's duration (reuse `market/orderflow/profile.py` bucket logic; re-anchor from session window to leg boundaries). Extract per-leg POC.
3. **Per-bucket delta** — net aggressor volume from the corpus trades' side field. This is TRUE per-trade aggressor delta, strictly better than the original's `request.security_lower_tf` lower-timeframe approximation; state this in the findings.
4. **Naked POC projection** — a confirmed leg's POC projects forward until first touch, then terminates.
5. **Volume anomaly** — bar volume > k × 20-bar average (k = spike-threshold param).

## Data

`data/corpus/<date>/databento_glbx_es.jsonl` — GLBX.MDP3 trades, ES.c.0; fields: price, size, aggressor side, ts_event. Two collections (verified via `manifest.json` notes, 2026-07-16):

- **Late-day collection**: ~253 days, 13:00–15:00 CT window, 2025-05-27 onward. Scale for intraday leg hypotheses; naked-POC carry-forward truncates at 15:00.
- **Full-RTH collection**: 08:30–15:00 CT — 2026-03-20, 2026-07-03, 2026-07-06, 07-07, 07-08, 07-09, 07-10, 07-13, 07-14 (9 days, growing as daily pulls continue). Plus 13 morning-only days (08:30–13:00 CT). Full-RTH days are where naked-POC and cross-session claims are testable end-to-end.

Run every hypothesis on both collections and report them separately — window truncation biases leg statistics.

## Hypotheses to score

- **H1 (naked POC)**: first touch of an untested per-leg POC produces a measurable reaction (bounce/rejection within N ticks / M minutes) at a rate better than a matched random-level control.
- **H2 (delta divergence)**: a leg extending to a new extreme while cumulative aggressor delta fails to confirm precedes leg termination at better-than-chance rates.
- **H3 (volume anomaly at extremes)**: anomaly spikes occurring within the final X% of a leg's range mark reversals better than anomaly spikes elsewhere in the leg.

Per standing rule (no pre-drop filtering): this is pattern-recognition measurement, NOT a classification gate on Steve's entries.

## Constraints

- Measured-architecture separation: comparison/indicator code in its own module (suggest `market/orderflow/legprofiler.py` or under `market/measurement/`); measurement outputs append-only under `data/measurement/`.
- Pure functions of trade list + named config constants, matching `profile.py` conventions.
- Sensitivity: sweep at least 3 swing-multiplier settings (e.g. 1.5 / 2.0 / 3.0 at ATR period 14) so conclusions aren't parameter artifacts.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Leg segmenter + per-leg profiler module with unit tests (deterministic: same trades in → same legs/profiles out).
2. Replay runs across BOTH collections without error; per-day results appended to the measurement store.
3. H1–H3 each reported with effect size, sample count, and control comparison, per collection, per parameter setting.
4. Short findings doc stating which (if any) of the indicator's claims survive contact with the data, noting the true-delta advantage over the TradingView original.
5. No repaint leakage: an audit check confirms no level is scored before its leg's confirmation timestamp.

title: Design: DataBento orderflow signal layer (Carmine triggers + orderflow-confirm)
description:
Scope + design the orderflow signal layer built off the DataBento feed — the trigger substrate the whole playbook system already leans on. Prioritized now because Steve's focus is orderflow for the next weeks-to-months (GexBot paused; GEX live-binding waits — see project memory / co-wh19 §10 item 2).

WHERE IT SITS: a new module consuming DataBento trades + MBP-1 (market/ingest/databento.py already streams TradeMsg / MBP1Msg / OHLCVMsg) and emitting orderflow signals. No orderflow model exists yet (market/signals/types.py has Signal/Bias/Regime/Level/Alert/Action — nothing for order flow).

WHY IT MATTERS — four consumers:
  1. Carmine setup recognition. The CarmineSetup taxonomy in strader/entities/singleton.py (failed_breakdown, level_reclaim, return_to_lvn, range_trap) is 'recognized from the feed' — orderflow IS that read.
  2. The orderflow-confirm (and return-to-lvn) Tier-2 entry tags in conditions.yaml.
  3. The day-classifier's mancini_carmine_confluence input (Carmine zones ∩ Mancini levels).
  4. Singleton setup triggers (SingletonSetup.trigger).

DESIGN QUESTIONS TO RESOLVE WITH STEVE (his domain / current focus — this is why it's a design bead, not a build):
  Q1. v1 orderflow primitive set? candidates: cumulative delta, delta divergence, bid/ask (footprint) imbalance, absorption, large-lot/sweep detection, LVN / volume-profile nodes from trades.
  Q2. How do the four Carmine setups map to orderflow patterns? (Steve owns this mapping.)
  Q3. Bar/window model: per-trade streaming vs time bars vs volume/range bars vs footprint bars. Must be deterministic + replayable (append-only corpus, history-is-the-value).
  Q4. Live + replay contract: one code path that runs on the DataBento Live stream AND the backfilled corpus (for study/measurement).
  Q5. Output shape: extend market/signals/types.py or a dedicated entity? How a recognized Carmine setup surfaces (SingletonSetup already models the trade idea).

BOUNDARY / NON-GOALS: no order routing, no automated entry; GEX stays out (GexBot paused); measured-edge / backtest deferred (co-wh19 §10 item 3). This bead is DESIGN — its deliverable is an approved design-of-record spec + prototype signal types, from which implementation beads spawn. Approach mirrors the playbook work (st-c71 / st-nk0): SP-lifecycle brainstorm → spec → implementation; form-first, DataBento as declared/replayable input, fully testable.
design:
REFRAME (2026-07-03, per Steve): all five are COO/Fable RESEARCH-AND-PROPOSE tasks, NOT decisions for Steve. Steve is not versed in the order-flow technicals and expects to LEARN the mapping (especially #2 and #5) from the model. This task is to be worked under the Fable model. Same working model as the coding: COO/Fable does the research and makes the technical calls; Steve validates.

Clarified five (plain language):

1. WHICH ORDER-FLOW MEASURES DO WE COMPUTE FIRST? Order flow = reading the actual buy/sell prints, not just price. Candidates: cumulative delta (running aggressive-buys minus aggressive-sells), delta divergence (price makes a new high/low but delta does not follow), bid/ask footprint imbalance (which side is lifting offers / hitting bids), absorption (large resting size eating pressure without price moving), sweeps / large lots (institutional-size prints), low-volume nodes (price levels that got skipped and tend to be revisited). Deliverable: research these, recommend the v1 subset with plain-English definitions and why each matters.

2. HOW DOES EACH CARMINE SETUP SHOW UP IN THE ORDER FLOW? The four setups: failed_breakdown, level_reclaim, return_to_lvn, range_trap. Each has an order-flow signature (e.g. failed_breakdown = price flushes below a level, sellers pile in, then delta flips positive and price absorbs and recovers). Deliverable: research Carmine method + general order-flow theory, produce the setup-to-signature mapping. THE HEART OF IT; deliver a spec AND a plain explanation Steve can learn from.

3. HOW DO WE SLICE THE STREAM INTO UNITS? (was 'bar/window model') Prints arrive one at a time; to compute the measures above we group them into units: by clock time (1-min bars), by volume (every N contracts), by price range, or as footprint bars (per-price buy/sell at each level). The choice changes which patterns are visible and must be reproducible so replaying history yields the identical result. Deliverable: research + recommend the unit model, prioritizing determinism / replayability.

4. ONE CODE PATH FOR LIVE AND REPLAY. The layer must run identically on (a) the live DataBento stream during the session and (b) the recorded corpus history (for study, and later edge measurement). Parity = same code, same output whether fed live or from a file. This is a design constraint to build in from the start, not an open question.

5. HOW DOES THE SYSTEM SAY 'THIS SETUP IS LIVE RIGHT NOW'? (Steve's read of #5, and the real question) Given the measures (#1) and the mappings (#2), the layer watches the flow and recognizes when a Carmine setup is forming/confirmed at a level, then surfaces it — feeding the singleton trigger, the orderflow-confirm tag, and the classifier's confluence input. This IS the 'recognize a suitable play from price action' capability Steve expects to learn from the model. Deliverable: design how a recognized setup is represented and surfaced.
acceptance_criteria:
- An approved design-of-record spec under docs/superpowers/specs/ covering: the v1 orderflow primitive set (Q1), the Carmine-setup -> orderflow-pattern mapping (Q2), the bar/window model (Q3), the live+replay contract (Q4), and the output shape + how it feeds Carmine recognition / orderflow-confirm / classifier confluence (Q5).
- Prototype signal-type definitions (frozen dataclasses) consistent with market/entities + market/signals conventions.
- Design questions Q1-Q5 resolved with Steve and recorded in the spec.
- Boundary explicit in the spec: no routing, no auto-entry, GEX excluded pending GexBot, measured-edge deferred.
- Follow-on implementation beads enumerated (built under those beads, not this one).
- Determinism + live/replay parity stated as an explicit design constraint.

MBP-1 NEVER backfilled — round-the-clock ES live access lands in weeks; quotes captured forward via live tee from then. Absorption runs trades-only (degraded, labeled) until quote capture starts. title: V metric definition — reconstruct net convexity from OPRA corpus
description:
Decide the canonical V metric for V-drop detection (st-r2o). jass watches 'net convexity' in GexBot State — trade-classified long-vol vs short-vol exposure, signed. We need an analog from the OPRA corpus (DataBento SPXW.OPT trades, 13:00-15:00 CT window, 250 days).

The question: can we reconstruct a meaningful 'net convexity' signal from raw OPRA ticks?

Options to evaluate:
1. Net vega aggregate — sum vega × signed_volume across all trades in window (call-buy adds +, put-buy adds +, any sell subtracts). Closest to jass's 'net vol' concept.
2. Net convexity (gamma-weighted) — sum gamma × signed_volume. Tracks acceleration of delta exposure, not just vol level.
3. Net delta exposure (DEX analog) — call and put sides tracked separately (per jass's DEX read methodology). More complex but richer signal.

Decision needed before detection script (st-r2o) is written. Output: a definition doc committed to docs/measurement/ that specifies the metric formula, sign convention, and rationale.
acceptance_criteria:

- Formula specified with sign convention (customer-buy = positive)
- Rationale tied back to jass's 2025-07-25 canonical entry
- At least one exploratory sample computed from corpus to validate the metric is non-degenerate

title: Strader: Day-type whippiness early-judgment study (V-days excluded)
description: Question (Steve): can we judge whippiness of the final 30 min from whippiness of prior afternoon periods? Method: 243-day ES corpus 13:00-15:00 CT in four 30-min blocks; whippiness as magnitude (range/path) and shape (chop/reversals); plus a 2:30-anchored CAUSAL fly study (241 days) centered on the 2:30 put-call-parity spot (no hindsight). All read-only analysis, nothing persisted. Findings in close reason.
close_reason: Answered. 'Whippy' splits into magnitude vs shape, opposite behavior. MAGNITUDE (range/path) persists strongly intraday — prior afternoon forecasts final-30 at path corr +0.74; calm vs hot prior afternoon -> final-30 range median 10.75pt vs 22.25pt (~2.1x). SHAPE (chop/reversals) does NOT persist (corr ~0). Causal test via 2:30-anchored fly (center on 2:30 put-call-parity spot, 241 days): the forecastable magnitude is a NO-GO tilt, not a buy signal — calm 2:30 -> fly pins 35% / dead 42% / ends ~4pt from center; HOT 2:30 -> pins 14% / DEAD 69% / ends ~8pt away. Earlier hindsight cut (fly centered on realized settle) falsely showed hot=deep-discount=buy; that was a centering artifact, corrected by the causal run. Whip (exit give-back ~$1.40) is unforecastable (corr +0.07) -> supports fast-cuts. Doctrine-consistent: calm=rotate/pin (flies OK), whippy=trend-away (flies at risk). Deferred (Steve pivoting to long singles): anchor-time sweep (2:00/2:30/2:45 'how early' curve); model actual dip-buy/rally-sell P&L. All analysis read-only, nothing persisted to repo.

title: Doctrine taxonomy reframe: proximity-to-late-day-window as primary filter (alongside or replacing canonical/community)

The tier filter solves an attribution-fidelity problem but doesn't help us FIND what's useful for the late-day measurement work.

## Proposed axis: late-day-window relevance

A simple secondary tag on each entry describing how directly it informs the late-day window we're studying:

- direct: entry literally documents a late-day mechanism (e.g. 2025-07-25 convexity-dump-then-ramp, 2025-04-09 0DTE-default-is-falling-vol, 2025-10-17 'literally all i do')
- adjacent: entry establishes infrastructure used by late-day work but isn't itself late-day specific (e.g. 2025-09-29/10-01 Classic vs State, 2026-01-02 mini_contracts schema)
- foundational: entry establishes definitions/conventions used across all timeframes (e.g. the first Jasper GEX-vs-gamma disambiguation entry, the customer-perspective closing-exchange entry, the John Kirby gamma↔convexity equivalence)
- 0HTE-specific: subset of 'direct' — the last hour or two of trading where 0DTE options dominate and vanna/charm overtake gamma (e.g. vanna_charm_ladder.md, the parts of 2025-07-25 that describe ~12:00-15:00 ET)

## Why this isn't just bolt-on metadata

The proximity filter is doctrinally generative — it tells us WHERE the gaps are. Steve observed 'there are surprisingly few posts targeting 0HTE.' If we tag entries by proximity, we can confirm or refute that empirically. If it's true, that's a research direction (file an entry of our own / commission analysis / look for material elsewhere — see also the 0HTE-services survey sub-agent running concurrently).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Decision on whether tags go inline at the top of each entry, as a separate index file, or both

- New entries (going forward) include the tag at creation time

title: John Kirby Discord 2025-04-21 — ITM call increase = high-confidence support signal
description:
Principal Q&A. Asker (community, unattributed) asks about large increase in ITM calls acting as support. John gives one of his most emphatic responses to date. Date 2025-04-21 8:19 AM.

Q: "For those of us who are new, does such a large increase in ITM calls usually act as support, as it did today?"
A (John): "YES. one of my favorite signals"

What's new:
- ITM call increase as a HIGH-CONFIDENCE support pattern. John explicitly elevates it: "one of my favorite signals." Not just "another bullish signal" — a setup he watches for specifically.

Mechanism (derived, not stated by John):
- ITM calls have high delta (~0.7-1.0)
- Customer long ITM calls → MM short ITM calls → MM must buy LOTS of stock to delta-hedge
- The MM stock-buying creates structural price support
- Larger hedge requirement per contract than OTM means stronger support force

title: Canonical-vs-measured comparison framework
description:
## Goal

Build the third box in the canonical/community/measured architecture: pure-function comparators that take a corpus row plus a canonical assertion and emit pass / fail / divergence outputs. This is the box that makes the canonical/measured separation operationally useful — without it, the canonical docs are just shelf decoration.

## Architecture context

The directory layout (per docs/gexbot/README.md) separates:
- **Canonical** (docs/{vendor}/canonical/) — verbatim vendor-published truth, immutable
- **Community** (docs/{vendor}/community/) — practitioner interpretations
- **Measured** (data/corpus/) — what we actually observed cycle-by-cycle

This bead adds the comparison layer.

## What the framework does

Given:
- A canonical assertion (e.g. "customer-long strikes act as walls — price gravitates toward them and stalls in declining-vol environments")
- A corpus row or window (gexbot.jsonl + schwab.jsonl + databento_opra.jsonl for one timestamp or window)

Emit:
- **PASS** — measurement supports the canonical claim (price did stall at the predicted strike under the predicted regime)
- **FAIL** — measurement contradicts the canonical claim (price blew through the predicted wall)
- **DIVERGENCE** — outcome doesn't fit either, often because a modifying canonical condition was not satisfied (e.g. "this was a rising-vol session and the canonical text says walls are vulnerable in rising vol — outcome was a failed wall, consistent with the modifier")
- **N/A** — preconditions for the assertion didn't hold (couldn't evaluate)

## Likely module layout

```
market/corpus/
  checks/
    __init__.py
    base.py             # Assertion / Check / Result types
    options_profile.py  # Checks corresponding to canonical/options_profile.md
    runner.py           # Iterate corpus rows, evaluate all registered checks
data/corpus/YYYY-MM-DD/
  check_results.jsonl   # Output: one row per (assertion × cycle) evaluation
```

## Initial check set (from canonical/options_profile.md)

1. **Wall behavior under declining vol** — at major_long_gamma strikes, does spot stall (defined: price approaches within N pts, doesn't break by M pts within K minutes)?
2. **Accelerator behavior under declining vol** — at major_short_gamma strikes, does spot pass through (define passes-through threshold)?
3. **Wall vulnerability under rising vol** — does the wall pass-through rate go up when ATM IV trajectory across cycles is rising?
4. **Short-side inversion under rising vol** — do major_short_gamma strikes start behaving more like walls in rising-vol sessions?

Each check needs explicit threshold definitions, regime detection logic (IV trajectory from Schwab chain), and falsification conditions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `market/corpus/checks/` package exists with `base.py` types
- At least one canonical assertion (the wall-under-declining-vol claim) implemented end-to-end
- Runner produces `check_results.jsonl` for one trading day of corpus data
- Output is structured (assertion ID, cycle ts, result, evidence fields) — readable with jq
- Each check declares its preconditions and falsification conditions in code, not just prose

## Non-goals

- Beautiful dashboards (CLI / JSONL output is enough)
- Auto-flipping canonical claims based on results (humans interpret)
- Multi-vendor checks (start with GexBot; pattern generalizes later)

## Why P2

Stand the corpus up first (st-1yp ✓), then accumulate days of paired data. Only useful to write checks once we have data to run them against. ~5-10 trading days of corpus data is enough to make initial checks meaningful.

title: GexBot State integration — probe, distillation, measurement harness
description:
## Goal

One-month evaluation of GexBot State ($150) as a vanna/charm intelligence layer for the late-day fly strategy. Build a thin, focused integration that emits a daily decision-grade signal Steve can act on without needing to read GEX ladders himself, plus a measurement harness that produces an empirical day-30 renew/cancel verdict.

## Architecture

**Layer 1 — Ingest.** `market/ingest/gexbot.py` provides `make_client()` (IPv4-only httpx with bearer auth, WSL IPv6 broken on this distro) and `fetch_state()`. API spec saved at `docs/gexbot/gexbot.spec3.yaml` (upstream: github.com/nfa-llc/gexbot-openapi master, v2.2.0). Base URL: `https://api.gex.bot/v2`. Auth: `Authorization: Bearer gexbot_custom_<key>`. Key in `.env` as `GEXBOT_API_KEY`. Rate limit 1 req/sec/metric per spec.

**Layer 2 — Distill.** `market/ingest/gexbot.py:distill()` consumes a state-tier response and emits a 4-tuple:
- `center_strike: int` — best EOD center, derived from `major_positive`/`major_negative` proximity to spot
- `regime: 'pinning' | 'trending' | 'unclear'` — derived from range width (V1 thresholds: <50 pinning, >100 trending)
- `confidence: 'low' | 'med' | 'high'` — derived from edge distance + zero-gamma transition risk
- `reason: str` — one plain-English sentence

V1 thresholds are educated guesses; real calibration comes after Layer 4 has data.

**Layer 3 — Pair with tape read.** TODO. Daily emission gets logged alongside Steve's manual tape-read center call. Format mirrors `gex_series.py` JSONL — one line per emission with timestamp, GexBot distillation, Steve's read, and (after EOD) the actual print.

**Layer 4 — Measure.** TODO. `data/gexbot_calibration/SPX_YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl`. After ~20 trading days, two numbers: (a) GexBot agent's center hit-rate within 5pts of EOD print, (b) Steve's tape-read hit-rate. Drives renew/cancel decision.

## Endpoints in scope (per spec; corrected after probe)

**Classic tier (table-stakes, paid by Steve's State sub):**
- `/SPX/classic/gex_zero` — 0DTE GEX (basic_response with `zero_gamma`, `major_pos_vol`/`major_pos_oi`, `major_neg_vol`/`major_neg_oi`, `strikes`)
- `/SPX/classic/gex_zero/majors` — key levels (classic-only; `/majors` does not exist for state endpoints — verified via probe 400 response)

**State tier (the differentiated value):**
- `/SPX/state/gamma_zero` — 0DTE orderflow-classified gamma. Top-level fields include `major_positive`, `major_negative`, `major_long_gamma`, `major_short_gamma`, `zero_gamma`. Strike-level data in `mini_contracts` array.
- `/SPX/state/vanna_zero` — 0DTE vanna (late-day reversal driver)
- `/SPX/state/charm_zero` — 0DTE charm (per-hour decay)

## Deliverables

1. ✅ `scripts/gexbot_probe.py` — connectivity diagnostic (LANDED commit 1643fdf)
2. ✅ `market/ingest/gexbot.py` — client + distillation module (THIS commit)
3. ✅ `scripts/gexbot_distill.py` — one-shot runner emitting the 4-tuple (THIS commit)
4. ❌ Pairing harness — Steve's manual tape-read input + post-EOD print backfill (next session)
5. ❌ Cadence runner — append-mode JSONL persistence at `data/gexbot_calibration/SPX_YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` (next session)
6. ❌ Day-30 measurement script — renew/cancel verdict numbers (after ~20 days of pairings)

## Acceptance Criteria

- ✅ Probe returns non-error JSON for /tickers + auth'd SPX endpoints
- ✅ Distillation produces all 4 fields from a real SPX state response — verified against live 2026-05-21 08:34 SPX data: spot 7404.52, center 7405, regime trending, confidence med
- ❌ JSONL persistence writes one line per invocation matching schema
- ❌ Pairing harness lets Steve log daily tape-read center + EOD print
- ❌ Measurement script consumes ~20 days and emits hit-rate verdict numbers
- ✅ Rate limiting respected (probe sleeps 1.1s between calls)

## Non-goals

- Websocket feed (REST polling is enough)
- Historical backfill via `/hist`
- Trade execution (evaluating signal quality only)
- Multi-ticker (SPX only for the eval)

## V1 threshold calibration notes

Initial thresholds are SPX/0DTE estimates, untested against outcomes:
- Range <50pts → pinning (tight 0DTE range, high gamma)
- Range >100pts → trending (wide range, low gamma anchor)
- Spot within 25% of an edge → center on that edge
- Spot within 5pts of zero_gamma → confidence drops to low (transition)

These get recalibrated once Layer 4 has 20+ days of paired outcomes.

## Authorizing context

CSO: COO-driven, see CLAUDE.md / project_coo-drives-strader-initial.md memory and feedback_make-brainstorm-decisions.md. Built off Steve's directive 2026-05-21 to absorb a one-month $150 GexBot State subscription after FlashAlpha free tier proved unusable. Day-30 renew/cancel decision is the deliverable, not the integration itself.

The remaining three deliverables (pairing harness / cadence runner / day-30 measurement script) were superseded by st-1yp (three-stream corpus) which expanded scope to Schwab + GexBot + Databento OPRA together rather than the original Schwab + GexBot pair. Bead st-1yp landed the cadence runner (scripts/corpus_poll.py), the structured persistence (data/corpus/YYYY-MM-DD/), and the per-day manifest. The day-30 renew/cancel measurement was promoted to its own bead st-cgb (canonical-vs-measured comparison framework, P2 deferred until corpus accumulates data).
